What SkyRPG is, how to install the pack and join the server, and what is inside it.

SkyRPG is a Hypixel SkyBlock-style RPG for Minecraft Java Edition 26.3, built on Fabric. You level skills, gather rare materials, craft better gear, fight bosses and clear dungeons, all the way up to the Ender Wyrm. Every gameplay system is our own mod. Other mods are only used for utilities.
This page tells you what you need to play, how to install it and join, and what the pack adds. Read First steps next.

Skyhaven is the hub: a floating village above the clouds. Everyone spawns here. It is safe: nobody can fight, take damage or go hungry, and blocks cannot be broken or placed. The shops, the bank, the Masters of each skill and the Wildgate are here. See Skyhaven.
The survival world is where you really play. Forests, caves, villages, dungeons, danger regions, the Nether and the End. Walk through the Wildgate or type /survival to go there. /hub brings you home. You return to where you left off.
If you die without a bed you wake up in Skyhaven. Your coins are kept on death.

Minecraft Java Edition 26.3 and Prism Launcher (free).
That is all. The SkyRPG instance brings Fabric Loader, Fabric API and every SkyRPG mod, and keeps them current.
The same SkyRPG version as the server. The instance updates itself, so you always match it.

Install Prism Launcher and sign in with your Minecraft account.
Download the SkyRPG instance: SkyRPG-Prism-Instance.zip. Don't unpack it.
In Prism choose Add Instance, then Import, and pick the zip. An instance called SkyRPG appears.
Launch it. The first start downloads the mods, so it takes a moment. A small window shows the progress.

From then on the pack updates itself from GitHub every time you launch. New and changed mods are downloaded, removed ones are deleted. You never need a new zip again. If you are offline, the game starts with the mods you already have.

If you cannot use the instance, the host can give you SkyRPG-<version>.zip. Unpack it. Inside is a mods folder and a HOW-TO-INSTALL.txt. You also need Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer and Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 from Modrinth. You must replace the zip after every update.

Add an instance: Minecraft 26.3, mod loader Fabric (0.19.5 or newer).
Right-click the instance, choose Edit, then Mods, then Add file, and pick every jar from the mods folder.
Launch.

Run the Fabric installer and pick Minecraft 26.3.
Copy every jar from mods into %APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods. Make the folder if it is missing.
Start the fabric-loader-26.3 profile.

Start the game, open Multiplayer and choose Add Server.
Type the address the host gave you.
Ask the host to add your name to the whitelist if you cannot get in.
The easy way is the Play SkyRPG button on the title screen, which joins skyrpgsurvival.falixsrv.me for you (no VPN needed). In Multiplayer, add that address yourself. See First launch and setup.

When you first appear in Skyhaven you get a short welcome in chat. Press K to open the SkyRPG menu and talk to Hollis Barrowmead at the tavern to start the questline. First steps walks you through it.

The SkyRPG title screen and the first-time setup: performance presets, shaders, resource packs, keys and the main settings.

The first time you start the pack, a short setup opens before the main menu. It takes about a minute and tunes the game for your computer. You have to go through every step: on the very first start there is no skip button and Esc does nothing, until you press Finish on the last step. Every step already has a sensible choice picked, so it is just Next, Next, and so on. After that you get the SkyRPG title screen, with a big Play button. Both can be opened again whenever you like, and then the setup can be closed at any time.
The title screen replaces Minecraft's. It shows the world's panorama under a navy tint with slow drifting stars, the SkyRPG name, and these buttons:
Play SkyRPG | Joins the SkyRPG server straight away. If no server address is set, it opens Multiplayer
Singleplayer and Multiplayer | The normal Minecraft screens
Settings | Minecraft's own options (video, sound, controls)
SkyRPG Setup | Opens the first-time setup again
Wiki | Opens this wiki inside the game. If the wiki mod is missing it opens the website instead
Mods | Mod Menu, when it is installed

The footer shows the pack version and the Minecraft version. On wider windows a What's new box lists the latest changes. It is fetched from the website when you start the game, and simply does not appear when you are offline.
It works from a small window to a 4K monitor at any GUI scale. You can press Tab and the arrow keys to move between buttons and Enter to press one, and screen readers read every button.

Play SkyRPG joins the server at skyrpgsurvival.falixsrv.me (no VPN needed; ask the host to whitelist your name). If it can't connect, the game shows "Can't reach the SkyRPG server. It may be starting up or offline: try again in a minute." with Try again and Open Multiplayer buttons.

The address lives in config/skyrpg/welcome.json in your game folder. Edit serverAddress to change where Play joins (for example localhost if you host the server yourself). Leave it empty and Play opens the Multiplayer screen.
If you prefer the plain Minecraft title screen, turn off SkyRPG title screen in K > Settings > Interface.
The setup has six steps. Use Next and Back to move between them. Every choice is applied straight away and saved. When you open it again later you can also close it with Close or Esc at any time.

Welcome. What SkyRPG is, in two lines.
Performance. Pick a preset. The one that suits your computer (from its memory, processor threads and graphics card) is named under the cards, and on the first start it is already applied, so you can just continue. Hover a card to see exactly what it sets.
Visuals. Switch shaders on and choose a shader pack (needs the Iris mod and packs in the shaderpacks folder), and turn resource packs from the resourcepacks folder on or off. Scroll the lists with the mouse wheel. Resource packs reload once when you leave the step.
Controls. The keys that matter: the SkyRPG keys (K menu, map, backpack, wiki lookup, spell wheel), zoom when Zoomify is installed, and movement. Click a key, then press the new one. Esc cancels and Backspace clears. A key shown in red is used by something else too. Open all key bindings opens Minecraft's full Controls screen.
Interface. The settings that matter most: themed chat, message spacing, the HUD, the minimap, the tab list and the SkyRPG title screen. They are the same settings as K > Settings, so they stay in sync.
Done. A summary of what you changed and a Play SkyRPG button.
Potato | Old laptops, integrated graphics | 6 chunks | 5 | Fast | Minimal | Off | 50% | 60 | On
Balanced | Most computers | 10 | 8 | Fancy | Decreased | Fast | 75% | 120 | On
High | Gaming PCs | 16 | 12 | Fancy | All | Fancy | 100% | 240 | Off
Ultra | Strong graphics cards | 24 | 16 | Fabulous | All | Fancy | 150% | Unlimited | Off

Minecraft then shows the graphics mode as Custom, because the preset sets more than the Fast, Fancy and Fabulous buttons. Every preset also sets the biome blend (0, 2, 4 and 6), turns off ambient occlusion on Potato, turns off entity shadows on Potato, and lowers the frame rate when the game is in the background (Potato and Balanced also do that when you are away from the keyboard).
If these mods are installed, the setup also uses them:

Dynamic FPS is switched on.
Dynamic lights (LambDynamicLights) go to off on Potato, fast on Balanced and fancy above.
Sodium and Iris are not changed beyond what the vanilla options already do (Sodium follows the view distance and the other options). Iris is driven for the shader choice.
Without Iris the shader list is hidden.
Zoomify adds its zoom key to the Controls step.
Mod Menu adds the Mods button to the title screen.
Nothing needs them: without any of these mods the setup only changes Minecraft's own options.

On the title screen, press SkyRPG Setup.
In the game, press K, open Settings, and use Show the setup again in the Interface category.
Type /welcome in the chat.
The setup only opens by itself once. It is remembered in config/skyrpg/welcome.json, in the setupVersion entry. Delete that line to see it again at the next start.
Your first hour in SkyRPG: the Skyhaven Chronicle tour, your first tools and your first coins.

You spawn in Skyhaven with nothing to do and a lot of friendly strangers. This page is a route through your first hour: which quests to take, who to meet, what to buy and where the first coins come from. Follow it and you will know every system you need for the survival world.

You appear on the Skyheart plaza, a little south of the golden fountain at the centre of the town. Nobody can hurt you here and nobody gets hungry. Take a minute to find your bearings with the minimap in the top right corner. Press M for the world map.
Press K to open the SkyRPG menu. The pages down the left are your Profile, Stats, Skills, Talents, Journal and more. See the K menu for all of them.
The questline is called the Skyhaven Chronicle. Every quest is a conversation with an NPC.

A gold ! over an NPC means they have a quest for you.
A grey ? means you are working on one of theirs.
A gold ? means it is ready: go back and talk to them to hand it in.

Right-click the NPC to talk. Click a choice, press Space to skip the typing, or press the number on a choice. Stay close to the NPC while you talk. Esc closes the conversation, and you can pick it up again later. Details are on Quests and the Journal.
Chapter 1 has 11 quests and pays 600 coins and 165 SkyRPG XP in total. It is a tour of the town in this order.
A Warm Welcome | Journal, then Hollis | Talk to Hollis Barrowmead in the tavern | 40 coins, 8 bread
Your Journal | Hollis | Open the Journal in the K menu | 30 coins
Find Your Way | Hollis, then Dorrin Saltmarsh | Visit the Provisioner at the Grand Bazaar | 40 coins, a compass
Safe and Sound | Dorrin, then Cassius Vellum | Visit the Banker at the Skyhaven Bank | 60 coins
Meet the Masters | Hollis, then Tamsin Deepholt | Meet the Mining Master | 50 coins, a stone pickaxe
Timber Talk | Tamsin, then Oswin Fernhollow | Meet the Foraging Master | 50 coins, a stone axe
Fields of Gold | Oswin, then Mabel Thornfield | Meet the Farmer | 50 coins, a stone hoe, 8 carrots
Patience, Love | Mabel, then Marina Saltwick | Meet the Fishing Master | 50 coins, a fishing rod
Steel and Nerve | Marina, then Kestrel Vane | Meet the Combat Master | 50 coins, a stone sword
The Artisan Bench | Kestrel, then Brannoc Ashforge | Meet the Blacksmith | 80 coins, 4 iron ingots
Through the Wildgate | Hollis | Step through the Wildgate | 100 coins, 32 torches
Where each NPC stands is on NPCs. The Master quests hand you a tool each, so you finish chapter 1 with a stone pickaxe, axe, hoe and sword and a fishing rod.
Chapter 2 starts outside, in the survival world. It has 12 quests and pays 2,290 coins and 365 SkyRPG XP. It asks you to:

Attune a waystone (right-click a standing stone, for example by a village bell).
Gather 64 Stone and 24 Coal for Tamsin, 32 Oak for Oswin, and 16 Carrots for Mabel.
Reach Fishing level 3 and gather 10 Cod for Marina.
Defeat 5 zombies and 5 skeletons for Kestrel.
Reach Mining, Foraging and Combat level 2 for Hollis.
Reach Mining level 8 and craft a Delver Pickaxe at the Artisan Bench.
Get a pet (Odessa Quill gives you a pup egg) and bring it along.
The quest rewards give you a stone tool for every trade. Better ones cost coins or the trade's own currency.
Tamsin (Mining Master) | Quarry Pick | 32 Glimmer Shards, no level needed
Brannoc | Iron Pickaxe, Iron Axe, Iron Shovel | 180, 150 and 90 coins
Brannoc, Mabel, Oswin, Marina and Kestrel also each sell a four-piece starter armour set: Prospector, Harvester, Woodsman, Angler and Vanguard. Prices are on Selling and shops and NPCs.
You do not have to buy anything. The stone tools get you through chapter 1 and 2, and you can save for the upgrades at the Artisan Bench later. See Crafting.
Coins sit in your purse, shown in the top left. They are kept when you die. Early on they come from:

Quests. Chapter 1 pays 600 coins and chapter 2 another 2,290.
Contracts. Three shared contracts a day, in the K menu. Mine 300 stone, chop 128 logs or harvest 128 grown wheat and you get 500 coins and skill XP. See Contracts.
Selling. Each Master buys the goods of their trade. A whole melon sells for 18, a pumpkin for 10, a mushroom for 10, a tropical fish for 20. Stone and logs are worth 1 and 2. See Selling and shops.
Elites. Gold-named monsters in the survival world drop 50 to 200 coins and an Elite Trophy worth 250.
Events. About every 60 to 90 minutes, when two or more players are on. See Events.
Contracts pay far better than selling the same materials. 300 stone sells for 300 coins, but the Stone Quota contract pays 500 coins and 300 Mining XP for the same job.
Put coins you do not need into the bank at the Skyhaven Bank. They earn 1% interest a day (up to 5,000). See Coins and the bank.

Press K and do chapter 1 (allow 15 to 20 minutes). Talk to everyone.
Open the Settings page once and glance at the HUD and Map options. See Settings.
Walk through the Wildgate with your stone tools and torches.
Do the chapter 2 gathering quests near the gate. Every one of them also levels a skill.
Come back by /hub or a waystone, hand the quests in and sell what you do not need.
Check the day's contracts in the K menu and take the ones you can finish.
Spend your first coins on the tool for the trade you like most.

Night in the survival world is dangerous. Mobs are levelled by distance from spawn, and monsters further out hit much harder. Stay close to the Wildgate until you have levelled a few skills. See Combat basics.

The whole path from day one to the Ender Wyrm, with rough levels and gear for each stage.

SkyRPG has a long ladder and no single route up it. This page lays out the path in eight stages, matched to the eight chapters of the Skyhaven Chronicle. For each stage it gives the skill levels to aim for, the gear that unlocks, and the places to go. The numbers are the levels the game itself uses: skill levels needed to craft or buy gear, the levels of dungeons and mobs, and the checks the questline makes.
Levels here are rough guides. You do not need to be exactly there. Read the gear tables as "you can start using this at about this level".
Every skill follows the same loop: gather, refine, craft, wear better gear, gather deeper.

Gathering gives skill XP, and every skill level gives stats and a talent point.
Materials are refined and crafted into gear at the Artisan Bench. Many recipes need the previous tier of the same item, and the new one keeps its name and enchantments.
Recipes unlock by skill level, and many mid-tier ones also need a collection tier. See Crafting and Collections.
Better tools reach better materials. Pickaxes and axes have tiers (I to VII), and a hard ore will not break with a weaker tool.
Tougher gear lets you survive further from spawn, where mobs have higher levels. That is where the rare drops are.
Surface, further out | +1 per 120 blocks from spawn, up to 30
Each level above 1 adds 8% health and 5% damage. Elites are three levels higher, with four times the health. A Blood Moon adds 10 more levels. See Combat basics and Danger regions.

2. First steps | First Steps | SkyRPG Level 2, Combat 5, Mining 8 | Near the Wildgate
3. Into the dark | Into the Dark | Combat 12, SkyRPG Level 5 | Forgotten Crypt, first slayers
4. The red lands | The Red Lands | Combat 18, Mining 14, SkyRPG Level 9 | Danger regions, Spider Hollow, Drowned Temple
5. The Deep | The Deep | Delving 5, Mining 18 | Underground layers, Dwarven Halls
6. Fire below | Fire Below | Combat 28, SkyRPG Level 20 | The Nether, Infernal Citadel
7. Ancient ruins | Ancient Ruins | Tier IV slayer, 64 Ender Pearls | Ruined Citadel, Catacombs
8. The void | The Void | The Ender Wyrm, SkyRPG Level 35 | The End, Astral Observatory
The checks are the levels the Chronicle's quests ask for. You earn SkyRPG Level from quests, collection tiers, skill levels, slayer levels and first boss kills. See Collections.

Goal: clear your first dungeon, start slaying, enchant something.

Reach about Combat 10 to 12 and SkyRPG Level 5.
Find the Forgotten Crypt (forests and plains, mob levels 12 to 19). Its champion is the Bone Knight and its boss is the Crypt Warden.
Talk to Morwen Ashgrave and start a tier I slayer quest. Tier I costs 1,000 coins and needs slayer level 0. See Slayers.
Talk to Seraphine Vael and enchant a piece of gear. See Enchanting.
Mining 8 | Delver's Pickaxe, then the Delver set at Mining 10
Combat 10 | Fangsteel Sabre (life steal), and the Fangguard set from Kestrel for Valor Marks
Fishing 10 | The Reefwalker set from Marina for Tidescales
Farming 8 | Fieldhand set and Sunwheat from Mabel, paid in Dew
Foraging 8 | The Barkguard set, and the Ironbark Hatchet (also needs Ironbark collection tier II)
Delving 5 | Warden's Shroud set, made from Crypt Warden tokens
Goal: leave the safe ground and take something from a danger region.

Aim for Combat 18, Mining 14 and SkyRPG Level 9 (the chapter's last quest asks for them).
Danger regions are the red zones on your map: the Blightlands, the Ashen Wastes, Frostgrave, the Mire, the Haunted Moors and the Shattered Highlands. Monsters there are 12 to 20 levels higher and drop region essences for region gear. /region tells you what is nearby.
Clear Spider Hollow (under dark forests and pale gardens, levels 19 to 26) or the Drowned Temple (oceans, levels 26 to 33).
Slayer tier II: 5,000 coins and slayer level 2.
Mining 18 | Skyiron Pickaxe (Tier IV) and the Skyforged set
Combat 18 | Stormedge (Thunderclap) and the Stormplate set
Farming 18 | Sunreaper Scythe and the Sunward set
Foraging 18 | Mistpine Splitter and the Mistwarden set
Delving 12 | Arachne's Carapace set, from Spider Hollow tokens
Combat 14 to 20 | Region gear: Mirewoven (14), Blightforged (16), Rimeguard, Cinderplate and the Rimecleaver (20), made from region essences
Goal: go underground and reach the Dwarven Halls.

The caves get stranger with depth, in four layers: the Glimmer Caverns (y 0 to 40, +4 levels), the Fungal Depths (y -20 to 0, +7), the Dwarven Halls layer (y -40 to -20, +10) and the Magma Rifts (y -64 to -40, +14). The dungeon called The Dwarven Halls (levels 32 to 41) sits under mountains, hills and forests, and its boss is the Iron Thane. Reach Delving 5 before the quest "Delver's Creed".
Mining 26 | Duskbore Pick (Tier V, Echo Sense) and the Deepwarden set
Combat 26 | Riftblade (Riftstep) and the Riftweave set (15% dodge)
Fishing 26 | Abyssal Rod and the Abyssal set
Farming 26 | Frostbite Scythe (also needs Frostberry collection tier III), the Frostgrove set, Emberpepper seeds
Foraging 26 | Willowcleaver and the Willowshade set
Delving 20 | Runeforged and Tide Regalia sets and the Tidecaller Blade
Goal: enter the Nether, find Hellforged ore and burn down the Infernal Citadel.

Combat 28 and SkyRPG Level 20 are the chapter's final check.
Nether mobs start at level 20. Make a portal and find the Ember Forest, the Bone Sea and the Obsidian Spires.
Mine Hellforged ore with a Tier V pickaxe. Blast it into Hellforged Ingots and craft Hellforged armour (Delving 30) and the Hellforged Pickaxe (Mining 40).
Fish for Magma Fish in lava (Fishing 20 for the quest, the Magmaline Rod at Fishing 40).
Clear the Infernal Citadel (levels 44 to 52). Its boss is the Magma Tyrant.
Mining 35 | Emberheart Pickaxe (Tier VI, Molten Core) and the Emberheart set
Combat 35 | Cinderfang (burning hits, life steal) and the Cinderguard set
Farming 35 | Cinder Scythe, the Cinderfield set, Moonmelon seeds
Foraging 35 | Emberbrand Axe and the Emberbark set
Goal: two big dungeons and the Slayer veteran.

Clear the Ruined Citadel (rare, mountains and peaks, levels 54 to 58). Its boss is the Fallen Knight.
Find the sealed stair in the Magma Rifts that leads to the Catacombs (very rare, y -60 to -40, levels 59 to 62). Collect three Ossuary Keys from the Bone Wardens to reach the Bonelord.
Finish a tier IV slayer quest (60,000 coins, slayer level 6).
Gather 64 Ender Pearls for Odessa.
Goal: the End, and the final boss.

Enter the End. Mobs start at level 40.
Explore the outer islands for the Void Gardens, Shattered Isles and Astral Fields. Astral Crystals drop Astral Shards.
Clear the Astral Observatory (levels 60 to 65). Its champion is the Astral Sentinel and its boss is the Star Warden.
Defeat the Ender Wyrm, a level 100 flying serpent with about 2,000 effective health. Kill the Ender Dragon first. Then craft Void Sigils at the Artisan Bench (Combat 40) from 16 Astral Shards and one of each dungeon trophy (three Sigils per craft), and use one in the End. Bring two or three friends: everyone who fights it is paid.
Turn its Wyrm Scales and Void Hearts into the Wyrmscale armour and the Voidreaver sword (Combat 50, upgrading your Starforged set and Starfall Blade). Roughly five fights with a party pays for all of it.
Mining 45 | Lumen Breaker (Tier VII, double ore drops) and the Lumenward set
Combat 45 | Starfall Blade (Starfall) and the Starforged set (crits heal you)
Foraging 45 | Starwood Greataxe and the Starwood set
Farming 45 | Moonlit Reaper, the Moonharvest set, the Starbloom Planter
Fishing 40 | Magmaline Rod and the Leviathan set
Combat 50 | Voidreaver (Void Rend) and the Wyrmscale set (dodge and life steal), from the Ender Wyrm's drops
The chapter, and the Chronicle for now, ends when you reach SkyRPG Level 35 and tell Hollis.

Keep every skill moving. Skill levels give stats, and each level adds 5 SkyRPG XP.
Enchant everything you can. See Enchanting.
Wear an accessory in each of the four slots. See Accessories.
Get a pet for the skill you are levelling. See Pets.
Never throw away rare materials. Prism Fragments, Heartstones and Dread Fangs have uses at the Bench and sell for a lot.
Do not rush the Nether. Hit stage 5 gear first.

The extra mods the pack installs for speed and comfort, the zoom key, how to turn shaders on, and performance tips.

Besides the SkyRPG mods, the pack installs a set of well-known Fabric mods. They make the game faster, add a few comfort features and let you use shader packs. All of them are client-side: they change how your own game looks and runs, nothing about the server. The pack keeps them up to date the same way it keeps SkyRPG up to date.

SkyRPG was tested together with every mod on this page (chat, K menu, HUD and minimap, tab list, effects, 3D item models, the Ender Wyrm and the griffins, the wiki), also with a shader pack switched on.
Sodium | A much faster renderer. More frames per second and smoother chunk loading.
Sodium Extra and Reese's Sodium Options | More video settings (clouds, animations, fog, FPS counter) in one tidy screen. Find it under Options, Video Settings.
Lithium | Faster game logic, which helps the built-in server and big crowds of mobs.
Entity Culling and More Culling | Skip drawing mobs and blocks you cannot see. A big help in the busy hub.
ImmediatelyFast | Faster drawing of the HUD, menus and text.
Dynamic FPS | Lowers the frame rate while the window is in the background, so the game stops heating your computer when you tab away.
Zoomify | Hold C to zoom in like a spyglass. Scroll while holding C to zoom further or less.
Mod Menu | A list of the installed mods, with a settings button for those that have one. Open it with the Mods button on the title screen, or the small icon in the game menu.
AppleSkin | Shows how much hunger and saturation food gives, in its tooltip and on the hunger bar.
Mouse Tweaks | Faster inventory handling. Drag with the left or right button to spread or collect items, scroll over a slot to move items, and hold the button to move whole stacks.
Controlling | A search box in the Controls screen, so you can find a key quickly.
Shulker Box Tooltip | Hover a shulker box to see what is inside.
LambDynamicLights | A torch or lava bucket in your hand, and lit mobs and dropped items, light up their surroundings.
3D Skin Layers | Your skin's hat and jacket layers get real depth.
Continuity | Connected glass and other connected textures, for resource packs that use them.
Iris | Shader pack support. See below.
The pack also installs the libraries these mods need (Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin, YetAnotherConfigLib, Cloth Config, Placeholder API and Searchables). You never use them directly.

Hold C. The view zooms in smoothly, scrolling changes how far, and letting go zooms back out. Zoomify has its own settings in Mod Menu (change the zoom time, switch between hold and toggle, make zoom move the mouse more slowly). Change the key under Options, Controls, Zoomify. A second key, F6, gives a stronger zoom that also hides the HUD.
Zoom works with a spyglass in your hand too. If you want zoom on the mouse wheel only, set the zoom key in Controls to Unknown.

Shaders add realistic light, shadows, water and clouds. They look beautiful and they cost frames, so they are off by default. The first-time setup (see First launch and setup) can switch them on for you. Three shader packs come with the pack:
Complementary Reimagined | Natural and close to vanilla, with good shadows, water and sky. The one we recommend. | Medium
MakeUp Ultra Fast | Soft light and nicer water for weaker computers. | Light
BSL | Bright, colourful and dramatic. | Heavy
To turn them on in the game:

Press I (Iris: shader pack selection), or open Options, Video Settings, Shader Packs.
Click a shader pack in the list and press Apply.
Press U at any time to switch shaders off and on again without leaving the game. R reloads them.

On the first start the shader takes a few seconds to compile. The game can freeze for a moment.
The Shader Packs screen has Shader Pack Settings for each pack. Lowering the shadow distance and quality is the biggest saving.
Our effects (spell and boss particles, the screen flash and shake) still show with shaders on, and the HUD, the K menu and the minimap are not touched.
Shaders ask a lot of your graphics card. If the frame rate drops, choose MakeUp Ultra Fast or switch them off.
More shader packs: drop a .zip into the shaderpacks folder of your game folder (Prism: Folder, Shader Packs) and pick it in the list.

Iris binds "toggle shaders" to K by default, which is the SkyRPG menu key. SkyRPG moves Iris's key to U the first time you start the game with both, so the menu and shaders do not fight. You can change it back in Controls.
Two small optional packs sit in your resourcepacks folder. They are not turned on until you choose them in Options, Resource Packs (or in the first-time setup):
Low On Fire | The on-fire overlay sits low on the screen instead of covering it.
Fast Better Grass | Grass blocks show their top texture on the sides, so grass looks fuller.
SkyRPG's own look (menus, icons, weapon art) comes from its mods and still works with these packs.

Use the Balanced preset in the setup. Open it again with /welcome or K, Settings.
Lower Render Distance first. It is the biggest saving. 10 to 12 chunks is plenty.
Switch Graphics to Fast and set Clouds to Off or Fast on a weak computer.
Give the game memory: 4 GB is the default of the pack and enough for most people. 6 GB helps with shaders. In Prism: Edit, Settings, Java, Memory.
Keep VSync on if you see tearing, off if you want the most frames.
Dynamic FPS only helps while the window is not in front. Alt-tab away when you are idle.
If shaders stutter, lower the shader's shadow distance and use Complementary Reimagined or MakeUp Ultra Fast.
Fancy extras you can turn off in Video Settings (Sodium Extra): animations and particles, and the LambDynamicLights settings.
All of these are files in the config folder of your game folder, and each mod also has a screen in Mod Menu or in the Video Settings:
Iris and the chosen shader pack | config/iris.properties (enableShaders, shaderPack)
The pack only puts its default settings in place the first time. After that your own changes are never overwritten by an update.

A tour of the hub: the plaza, the bank, the Grand Bazaar, the Arcane Library, Starwatch and the Wildgate.

Skyhaven is a floating town above the clouds, and it is where you spawn, shop, bank and meet the people who teach you the game. It is a safe place. This page walks round it by area, with coordinates so you can find things on the map. North is the negative Z direction, and the Skyheart plaza is at 0, 0.

Skyhaven is its own dimension, separate from the survival world.
Everyone walks 60% faster in Skyhaven, so getting from one master to the next is quick. The boost ends the moment you leave the hub.
Nobody can fight, break blocks, place blocks or take damage. Nobody gets hungry.
Your survival health and hunger wait for you: going back to the survival world (Wildgate or /survival) puts them back to what they were when you left, so the hub is not a free refill.
You can use doors, trapdoors, fence gates, buttons, levers, bells and the waystone. Other blocks, such as chests and crafting blocks, cannot be used.
Fields cannot be trampled.
If you fall off the island you land back at spawn.
Block items, buckets and spawn eggs cannot be used here.
/hub brings you home from anywhere. /survival takes you to the survival world, back to where you were.

The plaza is the middle of the town. A golden beacon fountain rises under the floating Skyheart, a spinning amethyst crystal ringed with purple shards. Eight runestones with banners stand round the edge, between four avenues, with cherry planters and benches facing the fountain. Hidden lights keep it bright at night.

You spawn on the plaza, a little south of the fountain. The Skyhaven waystone stands just to the left of spawn, at -6, 18. Attune any waystone in the survival world and you can travel between them and the hub from here. See Waystones and travel.
The avenue north of the plaza climbs to the raised Crown Terrace.

Skyhaven Bank, with a copper dome. Cassius Vellum keeps your bank balance and pays you interest. See Coins and the bank.
The Emberforge, where Brannoc Ashforge sells armour, iron tools, coal and anvils, and buys ores and stone. A public Artisan Bench stands in its yard, next to him.
The Mason's Guild, where Petra Quarrystone sells building blocks by the stack.
The windmill, with turning sails, on the north-west edge. The Mining Master, Tamsin Deepholt, stands near it.
Greenhollow is a working farm with fields, and Mabel Thornfield sells seeds and planters there. Further west the Mistfall waterfall pours from the island onto a small pond islet below.
Timberline Lodge sits among great trees. Oswin Fernhollow, the Foraging Master, buys logs and sells saplings, stumps and the Woodsman and Barkguard sets.

Just off the south avenue, on the lawn in front of the gazebo, stands the brainrot podium: statues of the three best brainrot collectors on gold, silver and copper pedestals, with their scores. See Brainrots.

The tavern, with a beer garden and a gazebo, is where Hollis Barrowmead gives out the Chronicle's first quest. The build calls the building the Gilded Gull. Hollis's shop is named The Lantern & Ladle. A bridge from the beer garden leads to the Arcane Library.

The first time you look through it you earn the Stargazer advancement and 500 coins. Only one person can use the telescope at a time.

Skyhaven has fourteen NPCs. Between them they run every shop, the bank, enchanting, slayer quests and the whole questline. This page lists who they are, where to find them and what each one offers. For full price lists see Selling and shops.

Right-click an NPC to talk. Most open a screen: a shop, the bank, the enchanting table or the slayer screen. They also greet you with a line.

A gold !, a grey ? or a gold ? over their head means a quest. See Quests and the Journal.

The Skyhaven Chronicle questline: eight chapters of conversations, markers over NPCs, objectives and the Journal page.

The Skyhaven Chronicle is the main questline. It has 8 chapters and 59 quests, and it teaches you the game in order, from saying hello to Hollis in the tavern to facing the Ender Wyrm. Every quest is a conversation with an NPC, so you never need a guide to know what to do next. The Journal in the K menu is where you read, track and re-read them.

Find the NPC. A quest giver has a floating marker over their head.
Talk. Right-click them. A conversation opens. Read it, then choose accept.
Do the objectives. The Journal and the Quest Tracker show progress.
Return to the NPC. Go back to whoever the quest tells you to, talk to them again, and choose the hand-in option. You get your reward then, not before.
! | Gold | The NPC has a quest for you to pick up, or someone to talk to
? | Grey | You are working on one of their quests
? | Gold | A quest is ready: go and hand it in
A gold ? outranks a gold !, which outranks a grey ?.
A conversation is a panel along the bottom of the screen: the speaker's face and name, text that types itself, and answer buttons above it.

Click, Space or Enter shows the rest of the text, then goes on.
Click an answer, or press its number key.
Esc closes it. Nothing is lost. Talk to them again to carry on.
Stay near the NPC. Walk away and the conversation closes.
Quests that have no giver start by themselves. A "journal entry" pops up on screen, read by the narrator, when you are out of a fight. You can read it, accept it, and the quest begins.
Talk | Finish a conversation with a named NPC
Visit | Find a place, such as a dungeon entrance, a danger region, a layer, a dimension, or a waystone
Collection | Gather an amount of an item after accepting the quest, or reach a collection tier. See Collections
Skill level | Reach a skill level
Reach level | Reach a SkyRPG Level
Kill | Defeat a number of a kind of mob
Slayer tier | Start or finish a slayer quest of a tier
Craft | Craft an item at the Artisan Bench after accepting the quest
Obtain | Have an item, or a pet or an enchanted item, in your inventory
Every quest pays coins and SkyRPG XP, and many add items. SkyRPG XP counts towards your SkyRPG Level, 100 XP a level. Quest rewards are a large share of it. See Collections.
Press K and open the Journal page.

Left side: the chapters, each with how many quests you have finished. Click a chapter to open it, then click a quest to read it.
Right side: the quest's story, who gave it, the "Return to" step, its objectives with progress bars, and its rewards.
Track points your waypoint compass at the next place you need to go, or at the NPC to see.
Re-read shows a quest's conversation again. Finished quests offer Re-read intro and Re-read hand-in.
Abandon appears on side quests, which can be given up. The Chronicle has none yet, so you will not see it.
A Quest Tracker box on the HUD shows the quest you track. It sits on the middle left by default and can be moved or hidden in the HUD editor. See HUD and minimap.
/quest track [id] | Track a quest, or your tracked one if you give no id
/quest abandon <id> | Give up an open side quest

How much SkyRPG XP all the quests pay is on SkyRPG Level: the maximum.

A tour of the hub. You talk to Hollis, open the Journal, meet Dorrin, the Banker, and every Master in turn, learn the Artisan Bench with Brannoc and walk through the Wildgate. Rewards are stone tools, a compass, bread and torches. See First steps for the full table.

Outside, in the survival world. You attune a waystone and do honest gathering work for each Master: 64 Stone and 24 Coal for Tamsin, 32 Oak for Oswin, 16 Carrots for Mabel, 10 Cod for Marina, and zombies and skeletons for Kestrel. Odessa gives you a pup egg (Combat 3) and asks you to hatch a pet. Brannoc asks for a Delver Pickaxe (Mining 8) and Kestrel for Combat 5.

Find and clear the Forgotten Crypt for Kestrel and craft the Cryptbreaker for Brannoc. Get an enchanted item for Seraphine. Morwen asks you to start and finish a tier I slayer quest. The last quest wants Combat 12 and SkyRPG Level 5.

Enter a danger region, carry 10 region essences for Odessa, craft a piece of region gear, finish a tier II slayer quest, and clear Spider Hollow or the Drowned Temple. It ends with Combat 18, Mining 14 and SkyRPG Level 9.
Descend into the Glimmer Caverns, the Fungal Depths, the Dwarven Halls and the Magma Rifts. Reach Delving 5 and Mining 18, and craft a Skyiron Pickaxe.

Enter the Nether and find the Ember Forest. Gather 64 Hellforged Scrap, fish 8 Magma Fish (Fishing 20), clear the Infernal Citadel and craft Hellforged armour. It ends with Combat 28 and SkyRPG Level 20.
Find the Ruined Citadel and clear it, clear the Catacombs, gather 64 Ender Pearls, and finish a tier IV slayer quest.

Enter the End, reach the Shattered Isles, clear the Astral Observatory and defeat the Ender Wyrm. The last quest, "The Chronicle, So Far", asks for SkyRPG Level 35 and pays 30,000 coins and 2,500 XP. More chapters will follow.

Gathering, crafting and kill objectives only count what you do after you accept the quest. Stone you mined yesterday does not count towards "Gather 64 Stone"; start mining once the quest is yours. The exception is "craft" objectives: if you already carry the item (say you made the Delver Pickaxe before Brannoc asked), that counts. A quest an NPC gives (a gold "Speak to ... to begin" box in the Journal) has not started until you talk to them, and tracking it points at that NPC.

The Ender Wyrm quest needs you to fight the Wyrm: kill the Ender Dragon, craft a Void Sigil and use it in the End. Everyone who fights the Wyrm gets credit for the kill, not just the player who lands the last hit. See The Ender Wyrm.

Timed competitions with a live leaderboard and coin prizes: how they start, how points work, and each event.

Events are short competitions that run for everyone on the server. A live leaderboard shows on your screen, the best players win coins and items, and the winners get a podium with confetti when it ends. They are a fast way to earn coins and a reason to try a skill you do not usually play.

Automatically. While two or more players are online and nothing else is running, a random event starts about every 60 to 90 minutes. The pool is Timber Rush, Monster Hunt, Harvest Rush, Glimmer Rush and Fishing Frenzy.
By an administrator, at any time. Admins can also start Sky Rings, which is never in the random pool.
When one starts you get a banner and a chat line that names the event and its length.
Everyone | Every player on the server. Just do the thing the event asks for.
Opt-in | Only players who join. Type .join in chat, or /event join. Leave with .leave or /event leave.
Five of the six events are open to everyone. Only Sky Rings is opt-in.

Players in creative mode do not score, and neither do spectators.
Blocks you placed yourself do not score. Break natural ones.
You cannot break blocks in Skyhaven, so go to the survival world to score in the block-based events.
Players who join late are in, from that moment on.

Each event has scoring rules. Every rule that matches an action adds its points, so one action can match more than one rule. A sea creature scores 1 for the catch and 2 more for being a sea creature, for 3 in all.
Your score is shown on the HUD. Players at the top of the board win prizes.
Ties share a place. Two players tied for first are both first, and the next is third.
Only players with at least 1 point can place or win anything.
Prizes are handed out the moment the event ends. Coin prizes go straight into your purse.
Some events also give a small prize to everyone who scored. Monster Hunt does.

A card on the HUD (top right by default) for each running event, up to three. It shows the countdown bar, which turns gold in the last minute and red in the last ten seconds, the top five players and your own row. Your row flashes and shows a "+N" whenever you score.
Chat lines and action-bar countdowns warn you before the end.
When the event ends, a winner board shows the podium with confetti, your place and your prize. You can turn it off in Settings under HUD. See HUD and minimap.
The Tab list also shows running events.
Chop the most logs in 5 minutes. Every log of any kind scores 1 point.
Warnings come at 2 minutes, 1 minute, 30 seconds and 10 seconds.
Zombie, husk, drowned, spider, cave spider | 1
Warnings come at 5 minutes, 1 minute and 10 seconds, with a banner at 2 minutes.
Harvest the most fully grown crops in 5 minutes.
Wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, nether wart, cocoa (fully grown) | 1
Mine the most ore in 5 minutes. Rarer ores and nodes score more.
Coal, iron, copper, redstone, lapis ore | 1
Gold, emerald, diamond, Skyiron and Duskquartz ore | 3
The prizes are the same as Harvest Rush: 150, 75 and 40 coins.
Catch the most in 5 minutes. Every catch scores 1 point, and a sea creature scores 3 in all. Prizes: 150, 75 and 40 coins.
Fly through gold rings above Skyhaven for 60 seconds. It is the only opt-in event.

Type .join in chat or /event join during the 20-second lobby.
Your inventory is saved safely on the server and cleared. You get an elytra and 64 firework rockets, and start gliding as soon as you are in the air.
Each ring you fly through is one point.
Your whole inventory comes back when the event ends or when you leave, or the next time you log in after a crash.
First place wins 100 coins.
The prizes are modest, but the skill XP and materials you gather during the event are yours to keep. Start with the skill you were going to play anyway.
Join Sky Rings the moment the lobby opens. The 20 seconds go quickly.

Admins can start any event with /event start <id> [duration], stop one, change the clock or scores, and turn the automatic schedule off with /event auto off. These are the same commands that run the shipped events.

Your purse and your bank: how coins are kept, the daily interest, and how to pay another player.

Coins are the currency of SkyRPG. You carry them in your purse, you can keep them in the bank at Skyhaven, and you can send them to other players. Everything that costs coins, from a pickaxe to an enchant to a slayer fee, comes out of your purse. This page explains how to move coins around, how the bank's daily interest works, and how to pay a friend.
Your purse is the coins you carry. It is saved with your character and kept when you die.

A small pill in the top left of your screen shows the purse. You can move or hide it in the HUD editor. See HUD and minimap.
The Profile page in the K menu has two tiles, Purse and Bank.
/coins shows your purse and your bank in chat. /coins <player> shows someone else's.
Large numbers are shortened to fit, for example 1.23B. Hover to see the full number.
Coins come from quests, contracts, events, selling things, and monster loot. See Selling and shops, Contracts, Events and Quests and the Journal.

Cassius Vellum keeps the Skyhaven Bank, at the north end of the town. Right-click him to open the bank screen. You must be at the banker to use it, because the server checks that you are still talking to him.
The screen has a card for each direction.
All (deposit) | Moves your whole purse into the bank
Half (deposit) | Moves half your purse into the bank
All (withdraw) | Moves your whole bank balance into the purse
Half (withdraw) | Moves half the bank balance into the purse
Deposit and Withdraw with a typed amount | Move exactly that many coins
You can type an amount in the box. Letters work as shorthand: 2.5k is 2,500, 1m is 1,000,000 and 1b is 1,000,000,000. Press Enter to deposit, or Shift+Enter to withdraw.
The screen also shows your last ten deposits and withdrawals with their times. Interest payments appear in that list as deposits.
Nothing takes coins from you when you die, so the bank is not a safe. Both the purse and the bank are kept. The reason to use the bank is the interest.
Your first login each day pays interest into the bank.
When | The first time you log in on a new calendar day
Where it goes | Into the bank, not the purse

The 1% hits the cap at a balance of 500,000 coins. Keeping more than that earns the same 5,000. You need at least 100 coins in the bank to earn a whole coin. Your very first login, with an empty bank, pays nothing. You get a chat line when interest arrives: "Your bank paid N in interest today (1%, up to 5,000)."
Interest is paid only when you log in, so missing a day costs you that day's interest. It does not stack up.
Put coins you are saving for something expensive into the bank at the end of each session. A balance of 100,000 earns 1,000 a day.
There are two ways to send coins to another player. Both do the same checks.

Pick someone from the list of online players. Narrow screens show the list first, then the payment panel with a back arrow.
Type an amount, or tap a preset: 100, 1k, 10k, Half or All. 2.5k and 1m work.
Press Enter, or click Send.
The page shows your purse counting down as the coins leave, and says "Sent N to Name" when it is done.

You cannot pay yourself.
The minimum payment is 1 coin.
You need the coins in your purse. Bank coins must be withdrawn first.
Big payments take a second click. On the Pay page, a payment of 10,000 coins or more, or of half your purse or more, asks you to click again within 4 seconds to confirm. The page says how much of your purse it is.
The receiver gets a "paid you" message and a chime. Each of you hears a sound.
Payments are logged on the server.
Big payment | 10,000 coins, or half your purse
Talent reset | Free once a day, then 2,000 coins

How to sell items, what each shopkeeper buys and sells, and the prices.

Skyhaven's shopkeepers buy what you gather and sell what you need to keep going. This page explains how selling and buying work, what each keeper takes, and what is on every shelf. Prices are in coins unless a column says otherwise.
There are three ways to sell. They all pay the same price per item.
Right-click a keeper who buys things. The shop screen has a sell panel on the right that lists what you carry that this keeper wants.

Click an item to sell all of it.
Click Sell all to sell everything this keeper wants.
Each keeper only buys their own trade. Mabel will not buy ore, and Brannoc will not buy wheat.
After you sell, a Buy back button appears. It returns your last sale at that keeper for the same coins, as long as your inventory has room and you can pay.
These work anywhere, with no keeper, at the same prices.
/sell or /sell hand | Sells the stack in your hand
/sell all | Sells every stack of the item in your hand
/sell inventory | Sells everything in your inventory and hotbar that has a price
/worth | Shows the price of the item in your hand, and of the whole stack
Armour you wear and your offhand are never sold. Backpack contents are not touched either.

/sell inventory sells everything with a price, including rare finds. A Heartstone sells for 15,000 and a Prism Fragment for 1,500, but both are worth more as crafting ingredients. A shopkeeper's Sell all button skips them, because no keeper lists them. Use /worth first if you are unsure.
If an item has no price, NPCs will not buy it. Most SkyRPG weapons, armour, tools and accessories have none, so there is no way to turn them back into coins.

Click an offer to buy one. Shift-click buys a full stack, and right-click lets you pick a number: type it, use the arrow keys, or choose 1, 8, 16, 32 or 64, then press Enter. You can buy at most a full inventory's worth in one go.

Offers you cannot afford show how many coins you are short.
Offers that need a skill level you do not have show "Needs Mining 10" in red.
Some offers cost items instead of coins, such as Glimmer Crystals at Tamsin or Dew Vials at Mabel. The cost shows as icons with counts, red where you are short. The items are taken from your inventory.
If your inventory is nearly full, you buy as many as fit.
Bought SkyRPG items come with their proper name, rarity and stats.
Stay within 10 blocks of the keeper. If you walk further away the shop refuses the trade.

Three shared contracts a day: how they are picked, how progress and rewards work, rerolls, and every contract in the game.

Every day the server posts three contracts: shared jobs such as "mine 300 stone" or "deliver 24 Skyiron Ingots". Everyone's progress adds up to the same goal, and when it is done everyone who helped gets the full reward. Contracts pay far better than selling the same goods, so check the board every day. Open it with K, then Contracts.

Three contracts a day for the whole server. A new set is posted when the date changes, with a chat line: "New contracts on the board! (K -> Contracts)".
They come from different trades where possible. You will usually see three different ones, such as one mining, one farming and one fishing.
Level gates. A contract that needs a skill level is only picked if at least one player who is online when it is posted has that level. Everyone else can still join in.
Shared progress. Everything every player does counts towards one bar.
Everyone who helped is paid. If you added even one point, you get the full reward when it completes, however much the others did.
Offline players still get paid. If you helped and logged off before it finished, you get your reward the next time you join, with a "Contracts finished while you were away" message.
Done contracts stay done until the next day.
/contracts lists today's contracts in chat. A HUD box named Contracts shows the progress of the ones that are not finished yet. You can move it in the HUD editor. See HUD and minimap.
Break blocks | Blocks you break count, such as ore, logs or crops. Blocks that players placed do not count. Some contracts only count fully grown crops.
Kill mobs | Kills of the named mobs count.
Kill Elites | Killing an Elite counts.
Catch | Any catch with a rod counts. Some only count sea creatures.
Deliver | Items do not count when you gather them. Open the contract on the board and press the hand-in button. It takes the items from your inventory, up to what is still needed.
Blocks broken in creative mode do not count.
Rewards are given as coins, skill XP, and for some contracts items such as Glimmer Crystals, Dew or Elite Trophies.

The amount varies. Each contract has a range, such as 300 to 600 stone. The board rounds it to a tidy number when it is posted.
Coins and XP scale with the amount. The tables below show the reward at the lowest amount. A contract that asks for double that pays double coins and double XP. Items do not scale.
Coins go to your purse and the skill XP is added at once.
You can swap an untouched contract for a different one for 500 coins.

It must have no progress and not be finished.
Each contract can be rerolled once. The replacement cannot be rerolled again.
The new one is never the same contract, and it prefers a trade that is not already on the board.
The 500 coins come from your purse, and are refunded if no other contract can be offered.
"Needs" is the skill level that someone online must have for the contract to be offered. "Anyone" means it can always be picked.

Gather items to climb collection tiers, earn coins, stats and recipes, and build up your SkyRPG Level.

Collections count how much of each item you have gathered from the world. Every collection has nine tiers, and each tier pays coins and SkyRPG XP. Some tiers also give a small permanent stat, and some unlock Artisan Bench recipes. The SkyRPG Level adds up everything you do in the game, and it is the number other players see next to your name in chat.
Open the page with K, then Collections.
A collection counts items you gain from the world:

Normal pickups from the ground, as long as no player threw or dropped them. Items you drop on death and pick up again do not count twice.
Blocks you mine with auto-pickup, and fishing and lava-fishing catches.
Harvests, logs and catches handled by the farming, foraging and fishing mods.
Items you buy, craft or take out of a chest do not count, and neither do items another player drops or throws to you.
There are 63 collections in five categories: Mining, Farming, Foraging, Fishing and Combat.
Every collection has nine tiers, I to IX. Reaching a tier gives:

Coins. The amount depends on the collection. Rarer items pay more.
4 SkyRPG XP.
A stat at tier V (+1) and tier IX (+2 more), in the category's fortune stat for gathering collections. See the tables below.
Recipes, for some collections. A locked recipe at the Artisan Bench shows "Requires Coal Collection III".
You get a notice and a sound when you reach a tier. Hover a row on the page to see all nine tiers and what each gives.
Common items need a lot. Rare items need a little. As an example, the Wheat collection looks like this.
Each collection follows the same shape. Stone is the cheapest (50 coins at tier I, 30,425 in all) and Leviathan Scale the dearest (400 coins at tier I, 243,400 in all).
Combat | +1, then +2 of the stat in the table below
The two steps add up, so a finished collection gives +3 of its stat.

Every skill, how XP and levels work, level rewards, milestone coins and talents.

Skills are how your character grows. You gain XP in a skill by doing what it is about (mining, chopping, fighting...), and each level gives permanent stats, a talent point and new things to craft and buy. There are seven skills, each capped at level 50. Open the SkyRPG menu with K for the Skills page, or type /skills.
Farming | Harvesting fully grown crops, melons, pumpkins, sugar cane and more | Farming
Mining | Breaking stone and ores (rarer ores give more) | Mining
Foraging | Chopping logs and stumps | Foraging
Combat | Killing monsters (tougher ones give more) | Combat basics
Fishing | Catching fish and killing sea creatures | Fishing
Enchanting | Binding enchants, applying and combining tomes, filling the Codex | Enchanting
Delving | Dungeon chests, secrets, champions, bosses and discoveries | Delving
Slayer levels are separate: each slayer boss (Grave Tyrant, Bone Marshal, Broodmother, Void Stalker) has its own level that you raise by killing that boss. See Slayers.
All seven skills use the same curve. The table shows the XP needed to reach each level in total.

Reaching level 10 takes 1,000 more XP than level 9. From level 21 each level grows by only about 2.7%, so the last step (49 to 50) takes 21,500. At a typical pace (about 2,500 XP an hour) one skill reaches level 20 in about 20 hours, 30 in 65, 40 in 125 and 50 in about 200 hours, before any Insight, minions or events. Level 50 is the cap, and the action bar shows "MAX" once you get there.

Seeing it: every XP gain shows above the hotbar, for example "+4 Farming (54/125)", and a level up shows a notice in chat with your rewards, talent point and new recipes.
Insight stats: a skill's Insight stat gives that many percent more XP, so 20 Farming Insight is +20% Farming XP. Every skill has one, and each can reach about +130% from the same kinds of sources (see Insight below).
Pets: your active pet earns 25% of the XP you earn in its skill, and 5% from the other skills (see Pets).
XP boosts: every Saturday and Sunday (server time) all skill XP is doubled. Admins can also start a boost from the console, for example /xpboost 3 2h for 3x XP for two hours. A gold bar at the top of the screen shows the boost and how long is left, and the biggest running boost counts. It multiplies after Insight, so 100 Insight on a 2x weekend is 4x XP. Type /xpboost to see what's running.
Minions: a Minion works a block for you and keeps half the XP until you collect it.
No wasted XP: blocks you placed yourself give no XP (see Crafting).
Each point of a skill's Insight is 1% more XP in that skill (XP × (1 + Insight / 100)). Every skill can reach about the same total:
The skill's tool (pickaxe, axe, hoe or scythe, rod, weapon) | Common 4, Uncommon 8, Rare 12, Epic 18, Legendary 24, Mythic 30 | Only while held
Each armour piece of a set for that skill | Common/Uncommon 2, Rare 4, Epic 6, Legendary 8, Mythic 10 | Up to +40 for four pieces
Lore enchant on the tool | 6 / 12 / 18 / 24 / 32 | Miner's Lore (pickaxe), Woodland Lore (axe), Harvest Lore (hoe), Tide Lore (rod), Battle Lore (sword)
Your active pet | 0.2 per pet level × rarity | +10 at level 50 Common, +20 at level 50 Legendary
The skill's level 20 talent | +10 | Deep Study (Mining), Farmer's Almanac (Farming), Old Growth (Foraging), War Journal (Combat), Old Salt (Fishing)
Scholar's Focus (helmet enchant) | 2 to 12 | Every skill, Enchanting and Delving too

Fully geared that is about +130%, so XP more than doubles. Enchanting Insight comes from Intelligence gear (each mage armour piece and wand gives it on the same ladder), Delving Insight from the Delver set and the Delver Pickaxe. Starbloom Tea adds +4 Farming Insight for 10 minutes. Minion XP is not boosted by Insight (see Minions).
Every level of every skill gives all of these:

Stats, listed per skill below. They are permanent and stack with gear.
A talent point for that skill (see below).
New recipes and shop offers: the Masters' shops and the Artisan Bench unlock things at set levels, and the level-up box lists the new recipes.
SkyRPG XP: each skill level adds 5 SkyRPG XP towards your SkyRPG Level (see Collections).
Coins every 5th level (see below).
Farming | +4 Farming Fortune, +2 Health | +200 Farming Fortune, +100 Health
Mining | +4 Mining Fortune, +1 Defense | +200 Mining Fortune, +50 Defense
Foraging | +4 Foraging Fortune, +1 Strength | +200 Foraging Fortune, +50 Strength
Combat | +0.5% Crit Chance, +1 Health | +25% Crit Chance, +50 Health
Fishing | +1 Fishing Speed, +1 Health | +50 Fishing Speed, +50 Health
Enchanting | +1 Intelligence, +0.2 Magic Find | +50 Intelligence, +10 Magic Find
Delving | +2 Health, +0.25 Magic Find | +100 Health, +12.5 Magic Find
Every 5th level pays coins equal to the level times 100: 500 coins at level 5, 1,000 at level 10, up to 5,000 at level 50. That is 27,500 coins per skill over its ten milestones.

Every skill level gives one talent point for that skill, so a maxed skill has 50 points. Spend them in the SkyRPG menu (K, Talents) on that skill's perks. Most talents have several ranks and cost one point per rank, and the stronger ones unlock at a skill level. Talents give stats and the same gear effects as items do, so they stack with gear. You can have a talent point left over, and there is no deadline to spend it.
A reset gives all of a skill's points back. It is free once a day, then costs 2,000 coins.

The full trees are on each skill's page: Farming, Mining, Foraging, Fishing, Enchanting and Delving.

Put your first points in the talents with no level requirement (the +Fortune and +Speed ones), then pick up the rare-find and double-drop talents as they unlock. The big ones appear at levels 20 to 30.

Combat XP comes from kills, and tougher mobs pay more: 6 for a zombie, skeleton or husk, 5 for a spider, 8 for a creeper, 10 for a witch or blaze, 12 for an enderman, 15 for a wither skeleton or ghast, 40 for a ravager, 100 for an Elder Guardian, 500 for a Warden, 1,000 for the Wither and 2,000 for the Ender Dragon. Farm animals give 1. See Combat basics and Mobs.

The Masters in the hub (Tamsin, Mabel, Oswin, Marina and Kestrel) sell gear and eggs at set levels, and the Artisan Bench has recipes at levels 8, 18, 26, 35 and 45 for each skill. Armour sets, Weapons and Tools list what each level unlocks.

Special crops and their growing conditions, planters, sprinklers, Dew, compost, meals, tools and sets.

Farming is the skill of harvesting fully grown crops. On top of vanilla crops, SkyRPG adds four special crops that only grow in the right conditions, planters that grow a crop on a timer, sprinklers, a currency called Dew, meals, and a ladder of scythes and armour. Level 50 is the cap (see Skills overview).

Crops only give XP when they are fully grown, and crops you plant yourself count. Melons, pumpkins, sugar cane, cactus and mushrooms count as soon as you break them, but ones you placed as blocks give nothing.
Wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots, melon, sugar cane, cactus, cocoa, nether wart | 4
Harvesting a planter gives XP too (from 1.5 to 14, see the planter table). The Farming Insight stat adds 1% more Farming XP per point, and each Farming level gives +4 Farming Fortune and +2 Health.

Every fully grown crop you harvest has a 15% chance to drop a Dewdrop (40% from melons and pumpkins, 50% from planters). Farming Fortune multiplies the amount, and gear such as the Sunward set (+25% in daylight) and the Bumblebee pet (+15%) raise the chance. Nine Dewdrops make one Dew Vial at a crafting table, and back again.

Dew is what Mabel Thornfield (Thornfield Produce, the Farming Master) takes for seeds, planters, sprinklers, compost and Fieldhand gear as your Farming level unlocks them. Dewdrops sell for 3 coins and Dew Vials for 27, but they are not in "Sell all", so you cannot sell them by accident. Use /sell for them.
Each special crop grows from seeds on farmland, in four growth stages, but only grows while its condition holds. The seed tooltip says which. Vanilla bone meal does nothing to them.
Sunwheat | Under open sky, in daylight | 1 in 150 from fully grown wheat, or Mabel | Sunwheat Sheaf
Frostberry | In a cold biome, or within 2 blocks of snow or ice | 1 in 200 from fully grown Sunwheat, or Mabel | Frostberries
Emberpepper | Within 4 blocks of lava, or in the Nether | 1 in 50 from Emberite ore, or Mabel | Emberpepper
Moonmelon | Only at night | 1 in 300 from melons broken at night, or Mabel | Moonmelon Slice (2 per crop)

Seeds: Sunwheat Seeds, Frostberry Seeds, Emberpepper Seeds, Moonmelon Seeds. Mabel sells four seeds at a time from Farming 8 (Sunwheat, 4 Dewdrops), 18 (Frostberry, 2 Vials), 26 (Emberpepper, 4 Vials) and 35 (Moonmelon, 8 Vials).

Rich Compost grows any crop one stage when you use it on it, special crops too, and ignores the condition. Mabel sells four for 6 Dewdrops from Farming 10, and the bench makes four from 4 Dewdrops, 2 bone meal and 1 Glimmer Shard.
Starbloom is different: it only grows in a Starbloom Planter. A Starbloom Seed (1 in 2,000 from fully grown Moonmelon) is needed to buy that planter.
Crops in the wrong conditions just stop growing. A Frostberry field near a snow block, or an Emberpepper field next to a lava pool, works anywhere in the world.

A planter is a box of soil that grows its crop on a timer, wherever you put it and whatever the light, biome or water. When it is ripe, right-click or hit it to harvest 1 to 2 of the crop (times your Farming Fortune), with Dew and rare-find rolls. It then starts growing again. Sneak and hit it with an empty hand to pick it up. Place planters anywhere outside the hub.

Ores, nodes, Glimmer, rare finds, pickaxe tiers and armour for the Mining skill.

Mining is the skill of breaking stone and ore. It pays Mining XP, drops Glimmer Shards (the Mining Master's currency) on top of the normal drops, and gates the best pickaxes and armour in the game. Level 50 is the cap and the curve is steep (see Skills overview).

Every block in this table gives Mining XP when you break it. Blocks you placed yourself give nothing (the game remembers player-placed stone and ore per chunk), except nodes, which are placed on purpose. Vanilla ores of the same kind give the same XP.
Granite, diorite, andesite, tuff, calcite, dripstone, mossy cobblestone | 1
Sandstone, red sandstone, terracotta (all natural colours) | 1

Coal, copper, iron ore, nether quartz ore | 5
Nodes give far less, from 1 XP for Coal and Iron up to 3.5 for Lumenite. They are a steady trickle, not a way to level. The Mining Insight stat adds 1% more Mining XP per point.
SkyRPG adds four ores to the overworld and one to the Nether. Each overworld ore comes in a stone and a deepslate version, and only chunks generated after the ore was added contain it.

Ingots and Duskquartz Shards pack nine to a block and unpack again at a crafting table (Block of Skyiron, Block of Emberite, Block of Duskquartz). At the Artisan Bench (Mining 18), four Prism Fragments make a Prism.
For the cave layers below the overworld (Glimmer Caverns, the Dwarven Halls, the Magma Rifts) see The Deep, and for the Nether see The Nether.
Every pickaxe has a tier, shown in its tooltip. A block that needs a higher tier than your pickaxe does not crack at all, and the action bar and the look-at box tell you which tier you need.
III | Iron, Prospector Pickaxe, Delver's Pickaxe
The gates are block tags, so a data pack can move an ore to another tier. Tools lists every pickaxe with its stats.
Glimmer Shards drop from almost everything you mine:

2 to 4 from every ore, vanilla ores included.
1 from a node, half the time.
1 from stone-like blocks (stone, deepslate, tuff, andesite, netherrack, basalt and similar), 10% of the time.

Mining Fortune multiplies shards: every 100 Fortune doubles them. Nine shards pack into a Glimmer Crystal and back at a crafting table. Shards sell for 2 coins and crystals for 18, but the better use is Tamsin's shop and the bench.

Mining Fortune drops the block's normal drops again: one extra copy for every full 100 Fortune, plus a chance of one more from the remainder (250 Fortune is two extra copies and a 50% chance of a third). It works on everything in the Mining XP table above (stone, sandstone, sand, gravel and the rest, as well as ores and nodes), but not with a Silk Touch tool, and never on blocks a player placed.
Mining Speed makes you break blocks faster. 100 Mining Speed is twice as fast.
Both come from gear, talents, set bonuses, enchants and your Mining level (+4 Mining Fortune and +1 Defense per level).

Nodes are placeable ore blocks you buy from the Mining Master. Break one for its drop, Glimmer and a little XP. It then turns into a dark husk that cannot be mined until it regrows. Sneak and hit it with an empty hand to pick it up again.

Skyiron, Duskquartz, Emberite and Lumenite nodes need the same pickaxe tier as the ores. The Node Keeper talent and the Mole pet make nodes regrow faster (never by more than half).
Every ore and node you break rolls for two rare finds, announced with "RARE FIND!":

A Prism Fragment with a 1 in 300 chance.
A Heartstone with a 1 in 3,000 chance.

Nodes are three times rarer for both, so real progress means going out to mine. Gear, talents and enchants that say "rare finds 10% more likely" raise the odds (+100% means twice as likely). A fragment sells for 1,500 coins and a Heartstone for 15,000, but the best gear needs them.

Everything you mine goes straight into your inventory, including Fortune's extra drops and Glimmer, and so do blocks that fall apart because of your break (the sugar cane or cactus above, a torch on the side). If your inventory is full the rest drops at your feet and the action bar tells you.

Chop five hard woods, grow them in the right places, farm stumps for Heartwood and fell trees with Treefeller axes.

Foraging is the skill of chopping trees. SkyRPG adds five hard woods that need better axes and only grow where their conditions hold, stumps you can place for a steady trickle of XP, Heartwood Splinters as a currency, and a ladder of axes whose Treefeller ability fells a whole tree in one chop. Level 50 is the cap (see Skills overview).
Every natural log you chop gives Foraging XP. Logs you placed yourself give nothing extra, and Treefeller never fells placed logs, so your log cabin is safe.
The Foraging Insight stat adds 1% more Foraging XP per point. Each Foraging level gives +4 Foraging Fortune and +1 Strength.
Foraging Fortune drops a log's normal drops again: one extra copy for every full 100 Fortune, plus a chance of one more from the remainder.

Each wood has logs, planks (they work in every vanilla wood recipe), leaves and a sapling that only grows where its condition holds. Bone meal does not work on them. Hard logs need an axe of at least the listed tier, the same way ores need pickaxes (see the tier list below).

Mistpine | IV | In a cold biome, or above y 120 | Spruce logs in mountains (1 in 125) or taigas (1 in 250), Oswin | 6
Duskwillow | V | Within 4 blocks of water, and only at night | Mangrove logs (1 in 167), oak logs in swamps (1 in 125), Oswin | 8
Emberwood | VI | Within 6 blocks of lava, or in the Nether | Crimson stems (1 in 250), a ripe Emberpepper (1 in 250), Oswin | 11

Saplings: Ironbark Sapling, Mistpine Sapling, Duskwillow Sapling, Emberwood Sapling, Starwood Sapling. Sapling drops come from chopping logs, not stumps, and the Lucky Bough talent makes them likelier. Emberwood is fireproof and its leaves glow, and Starwood leaves shine.
All five also grow naturally, in chunks generated after they were added:

Ironbark in forests.
Mistpine in snowy taigas, groves, snowy slopes, snowy plains, windswept forests and windswept hills.
Duskwillow in swamps and mangrove swamps.
Emberwood in badlands, savanna plateaus and windswept savannas, and in the Nether's crimson forests and wastes.
Starwood, the rarest, in cherry groves, meadows and flower forests.

An axe has a tier, shown in its tooltip. A log that needs a higher tier does not chop at all, and the action bar says what you need. Vanilla axes: wooden and golden I, stone and copper II, iron III, diamond IV, netherite V. A Woodsman Axe is only tier II, so you need an iron axe or better for your first Ironbark.

Heartwood Splinters are the Foraging Master's currency. Chopping gives a splinter 10% of the time (50% from a stump), multiplied by 1 + Foraging Fortune / 100. Nine splinters make a Heartwood Bundle at a crafting table, and back again.

Stumps are placeable foraging nodes you buy from Oswin. Chop one for its log, a little XP and a splinter chance, then it regrows. Sneak and hit it with an empty hand to pick it up. The harder stumps need the same axe tier as their logs.
The Stump Whisperer talent shortens regrowth by 6% per rank (never by more than half). Stumps are a steady trickle of splinters, not the way to level.
Every log you chop rolls for two rare finds, announced with "RARE FIND!":

A Golden Acorn with a 1 in 500 chance (sells for 2,500 coins).
Elder Heartwood with a 1 in 5,000 chance (sells for 25,000 coins).
Stumps are three times rarer. Gear, talents and enchants that say "rare finds 10% more likely" raise the odds, and +100% means twice as likely. The best axes and armour need them.

Bite cues, catches that go straight to your inventory, Fishing stats, Tidescales, rare finds, sea creatures, baits (one per catch), hotspots, rods, sets, Fishing Frenzy and lava fishing in the Nether.

Fishing is the skill of catching things. Every catch pays Fishing XP and may bring a Tidescale (the Fishing Master's currency) or a rare find, and sometimes the bite is a sea creature that you have to fight. A special rod even lets you fish in the Nether's lava. Level 50 is the cap (see Skills overview).
Fishing uses vanilla fishing, so the vanilla Lure and Luck of the Sea enchants still work on the rod. On top of the vanilla catch, SkyRPG adds:

Fishing XP: 8 for every catch (14 in lava). The Fishing Insight stat adds 1% more XP per point.
Tidescales: a 1 in 10 chance on every catch, multiplied by 1 + Fishing Fortune / 100.
Rare finds: a Abyssal Pearl with a 1 in 300 chance and a Leviathan Scale with a 1 in 3,000 chance.
Double Catch: gear, baits, hotspots and talents give a chance that a catch comes up twice.
Sea creatures: your Sea Creature Chance is the chance that a bite is a creature instead of a fish.
Each Fishing level gives +1 Fishing Speed and +1 Health. You never meet sea creatures in the hub.

Fish approaching: a yellow ! floats over your bobber while a fish swims towards it.
Bite: the mark turns into a bold red !!! and you hear a high "ding" (only you hear it). Reel in now. It works the same in lava.
Catch: reeling in a bite plays a short chime and the catch (fish, treasure, junk, Tidescales and rare finds) goes straight into your inventory like mined drops, with the pickup sound. The XP orb still comes to you. If your inventory is full the rest drops at your feet. A Double Catch gives you both. Sea creatures are mobs and come up at you as before.
The marks are the bobber's name tag, so nearby players see them too; the ding is only yours.

Fishing Speed | Fish bite sooner: the wait for a bite is divided by 1 + Fishing Speed / 100. 100 points halves it, 200 makes it a third, 300 a quarter. Your gear, bait and a hotspot all add up, and vanilla Lure still works on top.
Sea Creature Chance | The chance that your line pulls up a sea creature instead of a fish. You start with 5%.
Fishing Fortune | More Tidescales from your catches. Every 100 is one more.
Fishing Insight | Each point is 1% more Fishing XP.

Tidescales come from catches and from killing sea creatures. Nine make a Tidescale Plate at a crafting table, and back again. Marina Saltwick (Saltwick Tackle, by the pond east of the hub square) takes them for gear and eggs.

When the bite is a creature, it is pulled out of the water at you and attacks. You cannot miss it: a big warning sign and a SEA CREATURE! subtitle with its name and level appear in the creature's colour, with a splash at the bobber and a dramatic sound. The rare ones (Night Skimmer, Abyss Warden and the Cinder Leviathan) get a stronger version, and everyone within 48 blocks reads "<name> fished up <creature>!" in chat. Killing it pays Fishing XP to the player who fished it up (the numbers in the table, set per creature by its level and rarity), and Combat XP to whoever kills it: the body's normal kill XP plus half the creature's Fishing XP (a Drowned Sailor adds 12, an Abyss Warden 450). If you fish it up and kill it yourself you get both, each counted once; if a friend finishes it off, you still get the Fishing XP and they get the Combat XP. The killer also gets the Tidescales and the rare-find rolls. It leaves after two minutes. Which ones can come up depends on your Fishing level, and the odds are by weight. Health and damage are multiples of the body's normal values.
The Abyss Warden is an Elder Guardian body and the rarest catch. The lava creatures are in the lava fishing section below.
Your level only decides which creatures can come up. Sea Creature Chance decides how often one does, so rods, baits and the Deep Lure talent are how you meet more of them.

Baits are used automatically while you fish: no need to right-click them (doing so just reminds you). Carry them and cast: the bait improves that cast, and one bait is used up per catch. Casting does not use one, and neither does reeling in with nothing on the line.

Which bait is used: the one in your off hand first (put the bait you want there), then your hotbar from left to right, then the rest of your inventory. The bait is picked when you cast, and you see it as a small looping particle at the bobber: a worm bait sprinkles earthy specks, a glowworm bait soft glowing specks, an abyssal bait drifting black ink.

While you hold a fishing rod, a small Fishing Bait box near the hotbar shows the bait that would be used and how many you have left (or "No bait"). Move or hide it in the HUD editor (see HUD and minimap).

Now and then, near someone who holds a fishing rod, a hotspot appears on open water (on lava in the Nether, for the Magmaline Rod): a circle about 4 blocks wide, drawn as a turning ring of glowing particles with a light pillar in the middle and a floating label such as "Hotspot, +30 Fishing Speed, 2:41". It lasts four minutes, then fades. There are never more than two near you, a while passes between new ones, they need real deep water (no puddles) and never appear in the hub.

Each hotspot has one or two buffs: Fishing Speed, Fishing Fortune, Sea Creature Chance, Double Catch or Rare Finds. The buffs apply to a cast while the bobber is inside the circle, not to you: cast into it and your bait box shows "Hotspot: ..."; pull the bobber out and they stop. They add to your bait and gear.
