The final boss. The Void Sigil that summons it, its three phases and every attack, Void Echoes, and the Wyrmscale armour and Voidreaver sword it pays for.

The Ender Wyrm is SkyRPG's final boss: a long serpentine dragon that circles above its arena, dives at you, breathes void fire, calls Void Echoes and, in its last phase, brings down a storm of void bolts. It is the hardest fight in the game, and the most generous.
You call the Wyrm with a Void Sigil. Anyone can do it, no admin needed.
Crafting. At the Artisan Bench (Combat 40), one craft turns 16 Astral Shards and one of each dungeon trophy into 3 Void Sigils:
So one full set of trophies pays for three fights. Each fight spends one Sigil.

Using it. Right-click it in the End, once the Ender Dragon is dead and no Ender Wyrm (or summoning) is already running in the End. Otherwise it tells you why not. You can use it anywhere in the End, but remember that the Wyrm flies through blocks and its attacks need open ground: the main island is the natural arena, but keep away from the exit portal in the middle (stepping into it sends you home). The spot where you stand becomes the arena centre.

The ritual. The Sigil is spent at once and the void answers for about 6.5 seconds: a ring of light closes in on you on the ground, two spirals of void light climb into the sky, the ground rumbles harder with every pulse, the screen flashes violet, lightning cracks around you, and then the sky tears open and the Wyrm appears 28 blocks away and 18 up, circling the arena. Hold your ground. If everyone has walked away before it ends, the ritual fizzles and you get your Sigil back.
Fighting together. It is built for a party of two to four. Everyone is credited, see Rewards. Only one Wyrm can be alive in a dimension at a time.

If it all goes wrong. If every player in the arena is dead (or has left, or is in creative or spectator mode) for 30 seconds, the Wyrm loses interest and sinks back into the void, its Echoes vanish, and the player who used the Sigil gets it back (if they are online). So a wipe costs you time, not trophies. (Staff can also use /wyrm summon and /wyrm kill.)
The Ender Wyrm quest, from Hollis Barrowmead in Skyhaven, asks you to "Defeat 1 Ender Wyrm" and pays 25,000 coins, 2,000 XP and 16 golden apples. It unlocks after the Astral Observatory quest.
Health | 1,024 base, with half damage taken beyond that, so about 2,000 effective
Body | A long head and 12 body segments, about 18 blocks end to end

The Wyrm flies through blocks, so it cannot be hidden from by building (but it will not dive below the ground: it skims the highest block under it). For the first 2 seconds after it appears it cannot be hurt. Only its head can be hurt: hit the head, not the body. It only targets non-creative, non-spectator players within 100 blocks of the arena centre, and its boss bar shows to everyone within 160 blocks.

The Wyrm is always in one of a few states, and every attack is telegraphed by particles and a sound before it lands. Between attacks it circles the arena at about 18 blocks above the centre at a radius of 28 blocks (24 in phase 3). When its circling wait is up (6 seconds in phase 1, 4.5 in phase 2, 3.5 in phase 3), it picks the next attack.
I | above 66% | Single dives, 3 Void Echoes.
II | 66% to 33% | Faster. Dive chains of 2, 4 Echoes, a shorter wait.
III | below 33% | The fastest. Dive chains of 3, shorter wind-ups and the void storm.
At each phase change it roars, sends out rings, and summons Void Echoes immediately.

Dive | A line of soul fire from its mouth to you, and a ring on the ground around you. It rears for 1.5 seconds (1.1 in phase 3), then dives along the line. | Hits for its full attack and throws you up. Hits each player once per dive. Chains 1, 2 or 3 dives by phase.

Void breath | It hovers 17 blocks away, opens its jaws and gathers void light for 2.1 seconds (1.5 in phase 3) while the cone's edges are drawn in soul fire. | A cone of void breath 26 blocks long and 34 degrees wide, which slowly tracks you for 2.75 seconds (3.5 in phase 3). Each pulse (every quarter second) deals 30% of its attack and applies Wither II. Clouds linger where it hits the ground.
Summon Void Echoes | It rises over the arena while rings grow on the ground for 2.5 seconds. | 3 Echoes (4 from phase 2) step out of the rings, 6 to 12 blocks from you.

Void storm (phase 3) | A warning in chat ("The sky above the arena begins to split...") and 3 seconds of rising rings. | For about 8.5 seconds, void bolts fall at each player's position every 0.4 seconds, plus random bolts around the arena. Each is marked with a ring on the ground for a second before it strikes.
The attack choice at each decision is random, weighted by what is off cooldown:

In phase 3, if the storm is ready, there is a 50% chance of it.
If a summon is ready and few Echoes are alive, a 50% chance of that.
Otherwise 40% breath, 60% a dive chain.
Echo summons have a cooldown of 25, 20 and 16 seconds by phase, and the storm has a cooldown of about 50 seconds.
Void Echoes are named, purple endermen:

100 health, 12 damage, level 70.
They are persistent and hunt the player the Wyrm picked.
The Wyrm only summons more when few are left: none alive in phase 1, at most 1 in phases 2 and 3.
They disappear when the Wyrm dies.
Clear the Echoes quickly: more than one at a time cuts into the space you have to dodge dives, and the breath cone punishes standing still. Stay away from the soul-fire line the moment you see it.
The void storm's bolts are marked on the ground first. Keep moving sideways, and do not stand in a ring.

Everyone who fought it is paid in full, not just the player who lands the last hit: anyone who damaged the Wyrm, plus anyone who stood in the arena (within 64 blocks of the centre) for at least 15 seconds. Rewards go straight into your inventory (or to your feet if it is full), so nothing falls into the void.
1 Void Heart, and a 35% chance of a second | Every participant
A 5% chance of a Thunderclap scroll and a 2% chance of a Meteor scroll | Rolled separately for every participant
30,000 Combat XP | The player who dealt the most damage
A boss kill for your journal, SkyRPG XP (15 the first time) and the Ender Wyrm quest | Every participant
A server-wide announcement | The first time the Wyrm is slain on this server, and a smaller one for each kill
When it dies, each participant gets a ranking ("#1 ... damage to the Ender Wyrm") with their damage.
Wyrm Scales and Void Hearts are the materials for the best gear in the game, made at the Artisan Bench (Combat 50) by upgrading your best piece of the previous tier. Your enchantments carry over.
Wyrmscale Crown | 1 Starforged Crown, 10 Wyrm Scale, 1 Void Heart
Wyrmscale Hauberk | 1 Starforged Aegis, 16 Wyrm Scale, 2 Void Heart
Wyrmscale Greaves | 1 Starforged Greaves, 14 Wyrm Scale, 1 Void Heart
Wyrmscale Treads | 1 Starforged Treads, 8 Wyrm Scale, 1 Void Heart
Voidreaver | 1 Starfall Blade, 24 Wyrm Scale, 3 Void Heart, 8 Astral Shard
A full set plus the sword is 72 Wyrm Scales and 8 Void Hearts, about five fights with a party. See Armour Sets and Weapons for the stats and the set bonus.

Wyrm Scales sell for 1,200 coins and Void Hearts for 20,000, but you will want to keep them.

Five pets, one per skill: how to get them, rarities, stats, perks, levelling and the Pets page.

Pets are small companions that float at your shoulder and give you stats while they are out. There is one kind of pet for each of five skills, and your pet levels up as you earn XP in its skill. At levels 25 and 50 it unlocks a perk. You keep a collection of pets in storage and swap the one that is out whenever you like.
Every pet also gives 0.2 Insight per level in its skill, times its rarity bonus: +10 at level 50 Common, +20 at level 50 Legendary.
Mole | Mining | +2 Mining Speed, +0.8 Mining Fortune | Nodes you mine regrow 15% faster | A free Echo Sense every minute
Bumblebee | Farming | +1.6 Farming Fortune, +0.2 Speed | 15% more Dewdrops | Crops within 4 blocks of you grow faster
Owl | Foraging | +1.6 Foraging Fortune, +0.2 Speed | Falls 3 blocks further do not hurt | Rare finds from logs 50% more likely
Wolf Pup | Combat | +0.8 Strength, +0.6 Crit Damage | Heals 2% of the melee damage you deal | Critical hits heal 3% of your health
Otter | Fishing | +0.8 Fishing Speed, +0.08% Sea Creature Chance | 5% chance a catch comes up twice | Breathe and swim easily underwater
Jack o'Lantern | Farming | +1.4 Farming Fortune, +0.6 Strength | Rare crop finds 25% more likely | Heals 2% of the melee damage you deal
Stats grow with level, so a pet is worth more the longer you keep it. Only the pet that is out gives stats, perks and earns XP.
A pet's rarity is rolled when its egg hatches and never changes. It multiplies the pet's stats:

At level 50 the stats from the table are 50 times the per-level numbers, then multiplied by the rarity. A Common Mole gives 100 Mining Speed and 40 Mining Fortune, and a Legendary Mole gives 200 and 80.
Pets come from eggs. Right-click an egg to hatch it straight into your pet storage.
Mole Egg | Mole | Tamsin Deepholt, 48 Glimmer Crystals, Mining 10
Bumblebee Egg | Bumblebee | Mabel Thornfield, 6 Dew Vials, Farming 10
Owl Egg | Owl | Oswin Fernhollow, 6 Heartwood Bundles, Foraging 10
Wolf Pup Egg | Wolf Pup | Kestrel Vane, 64 Valor Marks, Combat 10
Otter Egg | Otter | Marina Saltwick, 6 Tidescale Plates, Fishing 10
Golden Pet Egg | A random pet, Rare or better | Boss drops and dungeon vaults and reward chests
(no egg) | Jack o'Lantern | Only from the Hallow's Crate: Epic (pink tier) or Legendary (gold tier). See Crates

The Golden Pet Egg is a 6% bonus drop from the world bosses (the Hollow King and the Mother of Thorns), and also drops from dungeon bosses' reward loot, and from dungeon vaults and secret chests (see World bosses and Dungeons overview).
A pet's level goes from 1 to 50. The XP it needs grows quickly: 250 times (level minus 1) squared in total, so level 10 is 20,250 XP, level 25 is 144,000 XP and level 50 is 600,250 XP.

Your active pet earns 25% of the XP you earn in its skill, and 5% of the XP from other skills.
Stored pets keep their level and XP, but do not earn any.
At level 25 and 50 you get a chat notice with the new perk. At level 50 it shows MAX LEVEL.
A pet earns XP while you play, so equip the pet for what you are about to do (a Mole for mining, an Otter for fishing). Switching is free, and the others keep what they have.
You keep your pets in pet storage, a saved list of 30 pets (the server can change this number).

Right-click a pet item to move it into storage. If no pet is out, it also goes out.
Eggs hatch straight into storage. A full storage will not hatch an egg, so make room first.
The pet that is out floats over your shoulder for everyone to see.
Pet items already in your inventory stay items until you right-click them.

Open it from the SkyRPG menu (K). It shows a live 3D preview of the selected pet (it turns slowly and leans towards the mouse) with its rarity, name, level and XP bar. On the right you see its skill, stats and perks, then your pet storage with a count like 12 / 30: a grid with the active pet (green mark) and every stored pet, with rarity border, icon, name and level.
Click a pet to select it, then use the buttons:

Equip puts it out (the old pet goes back to its place in storage).
Unequip puts the active pet back in storage.
Take out moves it into your inventory as an item, to trade or give away. It is blocked while your inventory is full.
/pet give <player> <type> <rarity> | Operators only: adds a pet to someone's storage

The pet is a real 3D model beside your right shoulder, for everyone, in third person and in the inventory and K-menu previews. Each kind has its own look: the Mole wears a miner's helmet with a lamp, the Bumblebee has fuzzy translucent wings, the Owl has big eyes and ear tufts, the Wolf Pup has floppy ears and a wagging tail, and the Otter holds a pebble or a fish.

Rarity changes the look too: Common is plain, Uncommon and Rare change colours and add small accessories (a flower, a bandana, a sprig, a pickaxe, goggles), Epic adds a bigger accessory, and Legendary adds a crown or halo and a glow. A pet also gives off a rarity-coloured aura for nearby players. It trails slightly behind you when you move and leans into the movement.

Griffins: finding nests, taming, the stable and Mounts page, riding and flight, stamina and the ten colours.

Griffins are SkyRPG's first mount: an eagle's head, ruff and wings on a lion's body. You tame one in the wild, keep it in a stable as a Griffin Whistle, call it when you need it, and ride it across the sky. There are ten colours in four rarities, and the rarest are worth hunting for.

A griffin has 40 health and 7 attack damage and is a little bigger than a horse. It walks on the ground, flaps its wings in flight and spreads them to glide. You can also get a spawn egg for creative play (the Spawn Eggs tab).

Each new wild griffin rolls a colour by weight (98 in all). The colour sets the rarity, and the rarity decides how often you meet it. The name of its whistle takes the rarity colour (Common keeps its feather colour), and the Mounts page shows the rarity.
Common | Golden, Storm, Snow, Russet | 20 | 20.4% | Russet is a red-brown hawk front with a cream face and a rusty lion body
Uncommon | Midnight, Verdant | 6 | 6.1% | Midnight is near-black with blue-violet feathers and silver eyes. Verdant has teal-green feathers and a mossy olive body
Rare | Ember, Frost | 2.5 | 2.55% | Ember has a charcoal body, flame-orange feathers, glowing wing tips and pulsing eyes. Frost is pale ice-blue with glowing crystal-blue wing tips

Legendary | Prismatic, Astral | 0.5 | 0.51% | Prismatic is pearl white and cycles through the rainbow every 6 seconds with glowing trim. Astral is deep navy with twinkling star specks and faint constellation lines
Rare and Legendary wild griffins give off sparkles (more for Legendary), and taming one announces it to everyone on the server.

Wild griffins live around nests, which generate in the mountain biomes (stony, jagged and frozen peaks, windswept hills) but only where the area is part of the Shattered Highlands danger region (see Danger regions). A nest is a plus of five Griffin Nest blocks.

A nest keeps 1 to 3 wild griffins (fixed per nest) around it while a player is within 64 blocks. It checks every 5 to 8 seconds and spawns one when there are fewer than that number within 40 blocks.
Wild griffins wander within 14 blocks of the nest and are neutral. If you hit one it fights back with a claw and a leaping dive, from 5 to 18 blocks away, for 1.5 times its damage.
Wild griffins despawn when no player is near.

Feed a wild griffin raw beef, mutton, chicken, porkchop or rabbit. Each feeding has a 1 in 5 chance to work (the meat is used either way). When it works, hearts appear and the griffin turns into a Griffin Whistle in your inventory. A failed feeding shows smoke and a message.
The whistle holds the griffin's name, colour, owner and two small random stats, shown in its tooltip:

Speed: +0 to +15%.
Flight Stamina: +0 to +25%, which means more seconds of flight.
Both are the average of two random rolls, so middling values are the most common and the maximum is rare. The icon has the feather colour of the griffin.
Whoever uses a whistle becomes its owner, so whistles can be traded or given away. Take your whistle out of the stable to hand it over.
Right-click a whistle to add it to your stable, a saved list of up to 20 mounts (the server can change the number). If no mount is out, the right-click also calls it.

Only one mount is out at a time. Calling another puts the first back.
A mount goes back to the stable when you put it away, log off, leave its dimension, get more than 16 blocks from it without riding it, or 30 seconds after you get off.
If it would die, it is knocked out and flies home instead with its health refilled, so a mount is never lost.
It cannot be hurt at all while you ride it in the hub dimension.

Open it from the SkyRPG menu (K, Mounts). On the left is a live 3D preview of the selected griffin in its colour (it spreads its wings when the mouse is over it), with its colour, name, Speed and Flight Stamina. On the right are stat bars with the seconds of flight, then Your stable with a count like 4 / 20: a grid of mounts, the one that is out first with a green mark.

Call: it stands next to you (the one that was out goes back).
Put away: back to the stable.
Take out: moves it into your inventory as a whistle, to trade.
/mounts call | Calls your active (or first) mount
/mounts nest, /mounts griffin [color], /mounts tame, /mounts claim, /mounts storm, /mounts give <player> griffin [color] | Operators only: test and admin tools
Right-click your own griffin to mount it. Nobody else can ride it.
Air | WASD | Flies in the direction you face
Air | Sneak | Descends (it does not dismount you in mid-air; on the ground it does)
Flight holds at a hover when you let go. Riders take no fall damage, and neither does the griffin. If you get off in mid-air you get Slow Falling for 8 seconds.

Flight uses a stamina bar. At full stamina a griffin with no Flight Stamina bonus flies for 14 seconds, and the bonus adds to that (a +25% griffin flies for 17.5 seconds). The bar drains at different speeds:

Stamina refills on the ground in about 6 seconds. At zero the griffin glides down slowly at half speed and cannot take off or climb until it is above 10%. A Flight stamina bar above the hotbar shows your stamina while you ride (you can move it in the HUD editor, see HUD and minimap).

Not every griffin is friendly. The Storm Griffin is the boss of the Shattered Highlands: a much bigger hostile griffin that attacks the nearest player. It cannot be tamed or ridden and never becomes a whistle. See Danger regions.

Hover a tile to see what the stat does and where your bonuses come from: skills, gear, set bonuses, accessories, pets, collections and talents. See Stats.
A card for every skill with your level, an animated progress bar and your XP. Hover for details. See Skills overview.
A tab for each skill. Every skill level gives one talent point. Spend points on that skill's talents by clicking a card. Each card shows its ranks, what each rank gives and what it needs.
Reset gives the skill's points back. The first reset each day is free. After that it costs 2,000 coins. See Skills overview.

The overview has a card for each slayer line with your level, an XP bar, your boss kills per tier and any quest you are running. Click a line to see its level track (what each level gives and unlocks), the four tiers (the boss, cost, rewards, attacks and defences) and your own stats. See Slayers.
Today's three contracts with progress bars and rewards. Items to hand in have a hand-in button, and untouched contracts have a Reroll button. See Contracts.
The Skyhaven Chronicle. Chapters on the left, the open quest on the right, with Track and Re-read buttons. See Quests and the Journal.
A live 3D preview of the selected pet, with its rarity, name, level and XP bar. On the right are its skill, stats and perks, then your pet storage, shown as 12 / 30. Click a pet to select it, then:

Equip puts it out. The old one goes to storage.
Unequip puts it away.
Take out moves it into your inventory as an item, so you can trade it.
A live 3D preview of the selected griffin, with its colour, name, Speed and Flight Stamina. Below is Your stable, shown as 4 / 20. Select a mount, then Call, Put away or Take out. See Mounts.

Your party's members, each on a card with their face, a crown for the leader, online or offline, health and where they are. Click a member to set a waypoint to them. The leader can Promote and Kick. There are buttons for Party chat, Leave and Disband, a name field to Invite a player, and your pending invites with Accept and Deny. See Party.

Tabs for Mining, Farming, Foraging, Fishing and Combat. Each row shows an item's icon, your count, your tier, a bar to the next tier and what that tier gives. Hover a row for all nine tiers. See Collections.

Every title in the game. Earned ones are bright: click one to wear it, click it again to take it off. Locked ones are dimmed, say how to earn them and show a bar where the goal is a number. Tabs filter All, Earned and Locked. See Titles.

Your brainrot album: a card for each of the fifteen, with the 3D model of the ones you've caught and a ? for the rest. Click a card to see it up close and hear it say its name. J opens this page straight away. See Brainrots.
Pick an online player, type an amount or tap a preset, and send. Big payments take a second click. See Coins and the bank.
Every option, grouped by category, with a search box. See Settings.

The themed chat: level badges, name cards, emotes, stickers, pictures, showcase tokens, whispers, mentions and chat settings.

SkyRPG restyles chat. Every message shows the sender's level and a hover card, you can show off your gear in a message, and you can post stickers and pictures that appear right in the chat window. It also removes the "Not Secure" marks and report buttons from player chat. This page covers everything you can type and see.
A player's message looks like this:

The level badge is a star and a number in brackets, such as (* 42). The number is the sender's SkyRPG Level (see Collections). The colour changes every 40 levels: grey, white, yellow, green, dark green, aqua, dark aqua, blue, pink, purple, gold, red, and dark red from level 480. Hover a badge to see what the next colour is.
Titles. A title is a small pill before the name: an icon and a few letters in a colour. You earn titles in the game and pick one in the K menu (see Titles). An administrator can also give a player a staff title, which replaces the earned one.
The name has a hover card with the player's level, skills, purse, slayers, pet and held item. Click a name to start a /msg to them.
A stripe beside each message shows its kind: player chat, whispers, joins, deaths, SkyRPG notices and more. Hover a stripe for the time.
Joins, leaves, deaths and advancements have their own themed lines, with icons. A new player gets a welcome that tells them to press K.
Game messages about coins, skills, events and bank have an icon, a short bold tag in an accent colour, then the text, for example SKILL, COINS and EVENT.
Type one of these tokens anywhere in a message. It turns into a hoverable link that shows the real item tooltip.
[item] or [hand] | What you hold in your main hand
[offhand] | What you hold in your offhand
[armor] or [armour] | Every piece of armour you wear
An item shows its name in its rarity colour, with a rarity gem and, for stacks, x16. Empty hands show a grey [nothing].
Type a code and it turns into an icon or symbol. /emotes lists them all, and you can click one to use it. Among the codes:
The pixel icons draw as small sprites, and each skill has one. The rarity ones (:common: to :mythic:) show the same gems used on items.
Stickers are small pixel-art pictures. Type [s:name] (or [sticker:name]) and it shows as a picture in chat, such as gg [s:gg]. /stickers lists them, and a click puts a token in your chat box.
coins | coins raining onto a pile
An unknown name stays as plain text.

Run /share screenshot to show your newest screenshot to everyone. /share screenshot <file> shows a named one. The picture is scaled to at most 640 pixels and sent to every player with the mod. You can share one picture every 30 seconds. Players without the mod see the line without the picture.

Paste a link to a PNG, JPEG or GIF and it shows as a picture. Known sites load by themselves: imgur, Discord, Reddit, Tenor, Giphy and GitHub. Pictures from other sites show a "click to load" line if you chose Any site in the settings. GIFs show only their first frame. Pictures are capped at 4 MB.
Loading a picture from a link tells that site your internet address. Set Images from links to Off in Settings if you do not want that.

Click a picture in the open chat to see it full size. Esc or a click closes it. A message can hold up to three pictures. While one downloads you see [loading image...], and [image unavailable] if it fails.
Your name, or @yourname, in someone's message is highlighted and gives a soft ding. Whispers have their own softer ding. Both can be turned down in Settings.
/r <text> or /reply <text> | Reply to the last person who whispered you
Whispers have an envelope icon, a "From" or "To" label in their own pink-violet colour, and appear in the Whispers tab.

Party members have their own chat. /pc <message> sends one message to your party, and /party chat switches everything you type to the party until you run it again. Party lines have a green PARTY tag and a shield icon, and a crown before the leader's name. They show in All and in the Party tab. See Party.

SkyHelper is the server's assistant. Start a chat line with @skyhelper (or @helper) and a question, and it answers everyone in a few seconds. Its answers glow violet and teal with a few sparkles, so you can tell the AI is talking, and every item it names is a hoverable [item]. /ask <question> asks privately. See SkyHelper.

On the open chat window you get five tabs: All, Chat, Whispers, Party and SkyRPG. A tab is just a view of the same history. Closing the chat goes back to All. The Party tab holds only your party's chat and party notices, such as joins, leaves and invites. See Party.
All these options live in K, Settings, Chat. See Settings.

Every HUD box, the HUD editor, the minimap, the world map and the look-at and info boxes.

The SkyRPG HUD is a set of small boxes drawn over the game: your purse, your skill progress, a health bar, the minimap and more. Every box can be moved, resized or hidden, and each shows only when it has something to say. This page lists them all, explains the HUD editor, and covers the minimap, the world map and the info boxes from the Utilities mod.
Purse | Top left | The coin icon and your purse
Skill progress | Top left | Appears for about 8 seconds after you gain skill XP: the skill, the XP gained, your progress to the next level and the XP rate
Health bar | Bottom centre | Your health, in SkyRPG's units
Mana bar | Bottom centre | Your mana
Minimap | Top right | The area around you. See below
Info (coordinates, biome, time) | Top right, under the minimap | Position, biome, day and time. See below
Look-at info | Top centre | What you are looking at. See below
Waypoint compass | Top centre | A compass ribbon pointing to your tracked waypoint. Only shows while you track one. See Waypoints
Events | Top right | Running events with a countdown bar and the top five. Only shows during an event. See Events
Sidebar | Middle right | The scoreboard sidebar, including boards from events and admins, in SkyRPG's look
Contracts | Middle left | Progress of today's unfinished contracts. See Contracts
Quest Tracker | Middle left | The quest you track in the Journal. See Quests and the Journal
Slayer Quest | Top left | Your running slayer quest and its timer. See Slayers
Fishing Bait | Bottom centre, above the hotbar | While you hold a fishing rod: the bait that would be used with how many are left (or "No bait"), and the hotspot your bobber is in. See Fishing
Party | Middle left | A row for each other party member: face, name, health bar, a dimension tag, and Offline when they are logged off. Only shows while you are in a party. See Party
Flight stamina | Bottom centre | A bar while you ride a griffin. See Mounts
Blood Moon | Top centre | A timer while a Blood Moon is up. See Blood Moon
Brainrot catches | Top left | A card for a few seconds when anyone on the server catches a brainrot: the catcher and the brainrot turning in 3D. See Brainrots
Combat tag | Top centre, under the other boxes | A red "In combat" box with the seconds left (it blinks in the last 3), only while you are in combat. See Combat basics
All of them are on by default. Boxes with nothing to show stay hidden even when switched on. The editor always shows them so you can place them.

Banners slide in at the top of the screen for big moments, such as a skill level up. They queue up.
Mob nameplates show the level and health of hostile mobs near you.
The winner board shows a podium with confetti when an event ends.
The vanilla hearts and armour row are hidden while the health bar is on screen. Switch it off to bring them back.
The XP text that normally appears above the hotbar ("+4 Farming") is replaced by the Skill progress box.
All of these have switches in Settings under HUD.
Open K, Settings, HUD, Edit HUD layout.
Scroll over a box | Resize it, from half size to double size, in steps of 0.1
Right-click a box | Hide it, or show it again
R with the mouse over a box | Reset that box
R with the mouse over nothing | Reset every box
Esc | Finish. Your layout is saved.
Boxes pin to the nearest third of the screen, so your layout keeps its shape when you resize the window. Each box also has its own on and off switch in Settings under HUD.
The minimap is a small map of your surroundings in the top right.

It shows the blocks around you, in the colour of their own textures, so paths, roofs and flowers are visible.
Other players are shown as their faces and you are an arrow.
NPCs and your waypoints appear as icons.
Zoom with = and -. There are five levels, from a quarter of a pixel per block to four pixels per block. The zoom is remembered for each dimension. In the hub it starts zoomed in.
By default north is up. Turn the minimap with you makes the way you face point up.
Cave view: when you are underground, and in the Nether, the minimap shows the floor around you instead of the surface, and gets darker the deeper you go.
Waypoints outside the view show as an arrow on the rim.
The minimap can be switched off in Settings under Map.
Press M to open the map of everything explored in this dimension, by you and by everyone else on the server.
Hover an icon | See what it is
Right-click the map | Drop a waypoint
Click or right-click an icon | Track, share in chat, or remove it if it is your waypoint

Zoomed in, names show under the icons. Every NPC is on the map with their face, name and role, even when they are too far away to load. Dungeons, waystones and danger regions show up as you discover them. Walking up to a dungeon entrance adds it to your map.

The map is shared. What you explore goes up to the server a few times a second, and the parts of the map on your screen are refreshed from the server every 30 seconds, so land another player has explored fills in on your minimap and world map. Each dimension has its own shared map, and the server keeps it in the world folder. Your own copy is also saved on your computer in the skyrpg/maps/ folder of your game folder, for each server and dimension, so the map still works offline in single player. See Waypoints.
A box at the top centre shows what you are looking at, up to 12 blocks away.

Blocks: the name, which mod it comes from, how grown a crop is, whether a mining node has regrown, and whether your tool can harvest it.
Mobs and players: their health, and a player's ping.
NPCs: their role.

Under the minimap. It shows your coordinates and the way you are facing, the biome, the day and the time on a 24-hour clock, and optionally the frames per second. Each line has its own switch in Settings under Info, and FPS is off by default.

Hold Tab for the SkyRPG player list: heads and ping on the left, info panels on the right, such as running events. Every player's SkyRPG Level badge sits before their name, in the same tier colour as in chat, for everyone online, near or far. Names themselves are plain white. Switch the list back to vanilla in Settings under Interface.
If the HUD feels crowded, hide boxes you do not use in the editor rather than turning the whole HUD off. Everything you hide can be brought back there.
The whole HUD can be turned off with SkyRPG HUD in Settings under HUD.

Named, coloured points on your maps and in the world: how to make, track and share them.

A waypoint is a named, coloured point that you save. It shows on your minimap and world map, and as a marker in the world, so you can find your way home, back to a dungeon or to a friend's base. You can track one to get a compass at the top of the screen that points the way. Waypoints are kept on your own computer, per server and per dimension. Joining with the Play button or from the Multiplayer list is the same server, so you see the same waypoints either way.
Want to show a spot to the people near you instead? Press the ping key (middle mouse) while looking at it: everyone in the dimension sees a marker with your name for a few seconds.
/wp is a shortcut for /waypoint. Without coordinates the waypoint is placed where you stand. Put names with spaces in quotes, such as /wp add "My Base".

If you add a waypoint with a name you already have, it replaces the old one and keeps its colour. New ones take the next colour in a cycle of eight: gold, aqua, purple, green, red, blue, orange and white.
Press M, then right-click an empty spot on the map. A small dialog asks for a name and one of the eight colours. Click or right-click any existing icon for a menu.
When you die, a red waypoint called Last death is added where it happened. The next death replaces it.
/wp add <name> [x y z] | Save a waypoint
/wp list | List the waypoints in this dimension, with distance and clickable Track, Share and Remove buttons
/wp track <name> <x> <y> <z> | Track any spot, without saving it
On the world map, click an icon to open a popup with Track, Share in chat and, for your own waypoints, Remove. This works for dungeon and waystone icons too.

On the minimap: a coloured marker. If a waypoint is off the edge, an arrow on the rim points to it. The tracked one is drawn larger.
In the world: a diamond with the name and distance, such as "Base 142m". It fades in as you get closer, from faint at 2 blocks to solid at 16. When it is off-screen or behind you, an arrow at the screen edge points to it.
On the world map: the same colour as everywhere else, with its name when you zoom in.
You can track one thing at a time. The tracked target:

Always shows in the world, with a white ring round its diamond.
Gets a compass ribbon at the top centre of the screen. It shows N, E, S and W, a diamond for the target, an arrow at the end when it is behind you, the name, the distance, and whether it is above or below you.
Is cleared when you get within 3 blocks of it, with a message "You've arrived at...", or when you leave the server.
Only shows in its own dimension.
The Journal's Track button uses the same system: it points your compass at the next place a quest needs you to go. See Quests and the Journal.
/wp share <name>, or Share in chat on the map, posts this in chat:

Players with the mod see clickable Add and Track buttons next to it. The coordinates are taken to be in the dimension the reader is in, so only share a waypoint from the dimension you are both in. Names are shortened to 32 characters.
In K, Settings, Map, under Waypoints:
Waypoints in the world | On | The diamond with the name and distance. The tracked one always shows.
Waypoints on the minimap | On | The markers and the edge arrows
Waypoint distance | 2,000 blocks | How far away a waypoint still shows in the world and as an arrow. 100 to 5,000. The top setting is Unlimited
Waypoint marker size | 10 px | How big the diamond in the world is, 6 to 24
NPCs and waypoints, under the same category, turns the icons on both maps on or off. See Settings.
Make a waypoint at your base, at dungeon entrances and at anything rare you find. /wp list then works as a quick way back: click Track and follow the compass.

Parties of up to 8 players: they are saved, show each other's health on an overlay, share a chat tab and cannot hurt each other.

A party is a group of up to 8 players who play together. A party is saved: log out, come back tomorrow, and you are still in it. Party members see each other's health in a small overlay, talk in their own chat tab, can set a waypoint to each other and cannot hurt each other.

Type /party invite <player>, or open the Party page in the K menu, type their name and press Invite.
They get a line in chat with clickable [Accept] and [Deny]. An invite lasts 60 seconds.
When they accept, the party exists. You are its leader.
Anyone in the party can invite more people, up to 8 in all. You can only be in one party at a time. Joins, leaves, kicks, promotions and members logging in and out are announced to the whole party.
/party invite <player> | Invite a player (60 seconds to answer)
/party accept [player] | Accept an invite. Say the inviter's name if you have several
/party promote <player> | Make a member the leader (leader only)
/party disband | Break the party up for everyone (leader only)
/party list or /party | Show the members and who is online
/party chat <message> | Send one message to the party
/party chat | Switch your chat to party chat, and back

The party stays together while members are offline. An offline member keeps their seat and shows as Offline on the overlay, with the place they logged out. If the leader leaves, the member who has been in the party longest becomes the leader. If only one member would be left, the party disbands.
Party chat and the Party tab
Party chat and the Party tab

Messages to the party and party notices (joins, leaves, invites) appear in chat with a green PARTY tag and a shield icon. They are in All and in the Party tab of the chat window, between Whispers and SkyRPG. The tab gets a dot when a party line arrives while you are on another tab. See Chat.
Party chat and the Party tab
Run /party chat once and everything you type goes to the party until you run it again. It also switches off when you leave the party or log out.
A small box on the left of the screen shows every other member, always:

Their face, taken from their skin, and their name. The leader has a crown.
A health bar with the numbers, in SkyRPG's units (the same as your own health bar). It is green, turns gold under half and red and pulsing under a quarter.
A small tag such as Hub, Nether or The End when they are in another dimension than you.
Offline members are greyed out, and their bar says Offline.
It is a normal HUD box: move, resize or hide it in the HUD editor. See HUD and minimap. It only shows while you are in a party.

Press K and open Party. Each member has a card with their face, crown, whether they are online, health, and where they are (dimension, coordinates and distance, or where they were last seen when offline).

Click a member to set a waypoint to them. See Waypoints.
The leader sees Promote and Kick on each member (Kick asks for a second click).
Party chat, Leave and, for the leader, Disband are buttons at the top. Leave and Disband ask for a second click.
Invite a player has a name field. Pending invites you have received show at the top with Accept and Deny.
Hold Tab. Party members have a green mark beside their face, and a Party panel lists everyone with their health.

Party members cannot hurt each other. The hit is cancelled, with no damage and no knockback. It covers melee, arrows and other projectiles (the shooter counts, not the arrow), thrown potions that hurt, abilities and area attacks, enchant effects, and a tamed animal hitting for its owner. You can still hurt yourself.
A few things are not stopped: poison or wither that keeps ticking after a thrown potion, fire, and TNT.

The Settings page: every category, every option and its default, and how to search and reset.

The Settings page in the K menu holds every option the pack adds, in one place. Options are grouped into categories with a search box on top, and changes take effect straight away. Settings are saved on your own computer, in config/skyrpg/client.json in your game folder, so they belong to you, not the server.
Open it with K, then Settings. It is the last page in the sidebar.

Categories are listed down the left, each with an icon. Click one to see its options on the right.
Search. Type in the search box at the top of the left side, and the page searches every category at once. It matches names, descriptions and keywords, so "ding" finds the mention sound.
Toggles switch on click. Choices step through their options. Sliders can be dragged. Buttons, such as Edit HUD layout, run an action.
Reset to defaults is a button above a category's list. It appears once you have changed something in that category, asks for a second click within 3 seconds, then resets the category.
Some options have sections, such as Look or Mentions in Chat, to keep long categories readable.

The in-game assistant: ask it anything about SkyRPG in chat, and it answers from the wiki in a few seconds.

SkyHelper is SkyRPG's assistant. Ask it a question in chat and it answers within a few seconds, using what this wiki says: where to sell something, how to craft an item, where a dungeon is, what a stat does, what to do next. It runs on the server's own computer as a small AI model, so it costs nothing and nothing you ask leaves the server.
@skyhelper <question> in chat | Everyone: your question and its answer
While it works, "✦ SkyHelper is thinking..." shows above your hotbar. The answer looks different from everything else in chat, so you always know the AI is talking:
SkyHelper lines show in the All and Chat tabs, with a light-blue stripe (see Chat). The glow needs the Themed chat box setting, which is on by default.
SkyHelper never runs commands itself. When a command would do what you asked, it offers it as a green [▶ /command] button:

@skyhelper invite PhilipSGamer to my party gives [▶ /party invite PhilipSGamer].
An operator asking @skyhelper make it day gets [▶ /time set day]. Anyone else is told only an operator can do that.

Clicking a button runs the command as you, with your own permissions, so a button can never do more than you could by typing it. Buttons only show to the player who asked, even when the answer is public, so nobody can get SkyHelper to put a button in front of someone else. Hover a button to see exactly what it runs.

SkyHelper sees what you are holding, what you carry and wear, where you are (the hub or survival world, the biome and any danger region), your health, mana, coins, skill levels, stats and the quest in your journal. So:

"this", "it" and "my item" mean the item in your hand. Hold a Dread Fang and ask @skyhelper how much is this worth?.
"What should I do next?" gets an answer for your levels, your gear and your quest.
It remembers your last three questions for 15 minutes, so you can follow up: "and where do I find that?"
It cannot give items or coins, or change the game itself; at most it offers a command button (see below).

Prices, who buys and sells what, and the /sell commands.
Recipes: SkyRPG gear at the Artisan Bench, and vanilla recipes (pistons, furnaces, anything) read from the game itself.
Where things are: dungeons, bosses, NPCs, regions, waystones.
How systems work: skills, stats, enchanting, pets, mounts, parties, wands and spells, Blood Moons.
Plain Minecraft questions (redstone, brewing, mobs).
It is a small model, so it can still get something wrong. If an answer looks odd, click [Wiki] and check the page. The wiki is always the final word.

You can ask once every 8 seconds, and one question at a time.
Questions longer than 400 characters are cut.
If SkyHelper is offline you get "I'm asleep right now". Try again in a minute; the server starts it again on its own.

SkyHelper is the skyrpg_helper mod plus a small service, tools/skyhelper/helper.py, which asks a local Ollama model (qwen3.5:9b by default). The server starts the service when it starts and stops it when it stops. The service reads the in-game wiki files, so every wiki rebuild teaches SkyHelper the new content.
/skyhelper status | Whether the service and Ollama are running (operators)
/skyhelper start | Start the service if it is not running (operators)

Settings are in config/skyrpg/helper.json: enabled, url, cooldownSeconds, timeoutSeconds, autostart, python and script. Every question and answer is logged to run/skyhelper/log.jsonl, to find answers worth improving. python tools/skyhelper/eval.py asks 27 test questions and checks the answers.
Earnable titles, small icon-and-text tags you wear before your name in chat and the tab list: all 32, how to earn each, and how to pick one.

A title is a small tag, an icon and a few letters in a colour, that shows before your name in chat and next to it in the Tab list: [* Deep Miner] Name: hello. You earn titles by doing things in the game, from reaching a skill level to defeating the Ender Wyrm. Once earned a title is yours for good. You wear one at a time.

Titles unlock by themselves. The game checks your progress every couple of seconds, so a title you already qualify for is awarded the first time you log in after the update: nothing you did earlier is lost. When you earn one you hear a chime and get a TITLE UNLOCKED message in chat with a [Equip] button. Your very first title is worn automatically.
A title's colour shows how hard it is: grey is common, green uncommon, blue rare, purple epic, gold legendary and pink mythic. A few have their own colour.
Two titles are hidden: they show as ??? on the Titles page until you earn them.

K menu, Titles page. Every title is listed. Click an earned one to wear it, click the one you are wearing to take it off, or use Take off title. The tabs filter All, Earned and Locked. Locked titles are dimmed and say how to earn them, with a progress bar where the goal is a number (for example 4 / 25). Hover a row for the full text.
Commands. /title lists your earned titles with an [Equip] button, /title locked lists the rest, /title set <id> wears one (press Tab to complete the id, or click the button) and /title clear takes it off.

Chat: between the level badge and your name, as a small pill: (* 42) [* Deep Miner] Name. Your name stays white.
Tab list: a pill after your name, in the title's colour. A long title is cut with "...".
Name card: hover a name in chat to see the title on the card.
An administrator can also give a player a staff title with /chat title (see Chat). A staff title replaces the earned one while it is set, and the earned titles stay saved underneath.

The highest SkyRPG Level you can reach with everything in the game today: level 230 (23,023 XP). The level has no hard cap, but every XP source is finite.

The highest SkyRPG Level a player can reach is level 230, with 23,023 SkyRPG XP in all. This page is worked out from the game's data files each time the wiki is built, so it follows every change to quests, collections, skills, slayers and bosses.
The level has no cap in the game, but every source of XP is finite. With all of it collected, 23 XP is left over towards level 231. More content later means a higher maximum.
23,023 XP at 100 XP a level is level 230, with 23 XP left over.
Each skill level gives 5 XP. Enchanting and Delving count like the others.
Each slayer level gives 10 XP, twice a skill level.
There are 63 collections with 567 tiers in all. A tier gives 4 XP unless its data says otherwise, which makes 2,268 XP. The tiers are listed on the Collections page.

The first kill of each boss pays XP once. A dungeon champion pays 20, 30, 40, 50 or 60 by its level (below 25, 40, 52 and 62, then 62 and up). Every other boss pays 15. A boss that exists as several mobs, like the Bone Warden, counts once. Everyone who takes part in an Ender Wyrm fight gets its first kill. Slayer bosses give no first-kill XP. See Bosses.
